pitfalls.zh: Could I 问自己能不能做，问对方要做用 Could you。
pitfalls.en: Could I asks about yourself; for the other person's action use Could you.

examples.text: Could I borrow your pen for a minute?
examples.zh: 我能借你的笔用一下吗？

examples.text: Could I open the window?
examples.zh: 我可以把窗户打开吗？

explain.zh: 想劝对方试试某件事，就说 Why don't you + 动词原形，字面是「你为什么不……」，其实是在给建议。语气比 You should 委婉，像顺口提一句，对方听得出这是好意，不是在追问原因。
explain.en: When you want to suggest something to the person you are talking to, say Why don't you and the base verb. It looks like a question about a reason, but it is really a friendly suggestion, softer than You should.

form.zh: Why don't you + 动词原形？
form.en: Why don't you + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: 后面用动词原形，别加 to 或 -ing。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb after it: not Why don't you to rest.

pitfalls.zh: 这是给对方的建议；一起做的事改用 Why don't we。
pitfalls.en: It tells the other person what to do; for a shared plan use Why don't we.

examples.text: Why don't you take a short break?
examples.zh: 你为什么不歇一会儿呢？

examples.text: Why don't you ask the teacher?
examples.zh: 你可以去问问老师呀。

explain.zh: 想提议一起做某件事，用 Why don't we + 动词原形，主语是 we，说话人把自己也算进去。意思接近 Let's，但多了一层商量的口气，等对方点头。
explain.en: Use Why don't we and the base verb to suggest doing something together: we includes the speaker. It means much the same as Let's, with more room for the other person to agree or say no.

form.zh: Why don't we + 动词原形？
form.en: Why don't we + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: 一起做的事用 we；只让对方做才用 you。
pitfalls.en: Keep we when you join in; use you only when the other person acts alone.

pitfalls.zh: 后面接动词原形，不接 to do。
pitfalls.en: The verb after we is a base verb, not a to-infinitive.

examples.text: Why don't we meet at six?
examples.zh: 我们六点见怎么样？

examples.text: Why don't we take the train?
examples.zh: 我们坐火车去吧？

explain.zh: 已经聊到某件事，想顺势推一句「那就……吧」，直接用 Why not + 动词原形，省掉主语。它像接过话头的小建议，比完整问句更轻快。
explain.en: When something has just come up in the conversation, Why not and the base verb push it forward as a light suggestion: then do it. With no subject, it sounds like a quick answer to an idea.

form.zh: Why not + 动词原形？
form.en: Why not + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: Why not 后面直接跟动词，不加主语或 to。
pitfalls.en: Go straight to the verb after Why not: no subject and no to.

pitfalls.zh: 它不是问原因，别用 because 来回答。
pitfalls.en: It does not ask for a reason, so it is not answered with because.

examples.text: Why not try the soup?
examples.zh: 尝尝这个汤吧？

examples.text: Why not come with us?
examples.zh: 跟我们一起去吧？

explain.zh: 两个东西比高低，形容词或副词前加 more、后面接 than：more careful than me。词太长不好加 -er 时就走这条路，把比的对象放在 than 后面。
explain.en: To compare two things, put more before the adjective or adverb and than before the second one: more careful than me. This is the usual route for longer words, which cannot take -er.

form.zh: more + 形容词/副词 + than + 比较对象
form.en: more + adjective/adverb + than + the thing compared

pitfalls.zh: 短词用 -er：bigger，不说 more big。
pitfalls.en: Short words take -er: bigger, not more big.

pitfalls.zh: than 后面要写出比较对象，句子才算完整。
pitfalls.en: Do not stop at more careful; than needs the thing you compare with.

examples.text: This book is more interesting than that one.
examples.zh: 这本书比那本有趣。

examples.text: She speaks more slowly than her brother.
examples.zh: 她说话比她弟弟慢。

name.zh: 最高级：most + 形容词/副词

explain.zh: 三个以上里挑出最突出的那一个，用 the most + 形容词，或在副词前加 most：the most careful driver。比较的范围常放在 in 或 of 后面说明。
explain.en: When one thing stands out among three or more, use the most before the adjective, or most before an adverb: the most careful driver. The group you compare with often follows in or of.

form.zh: the most + 形容词/副词（+ in/of 范围）
form.en: the most + adjective/adverb (+ in/of + group)

pitfalls.zh: 形容词最高级前要有 the：the most careful。
pitfalls.en: The adjective needs the: the most careful, not most careful.

pitfalls.zh: 短词用 -est：the biggest，不说 the most big。
pitfalls.en: Short words take -est: the biggest, not the most big.

examples.text: It is the most beautiful garden in the city.
examples.zh: 这是城里最美的花园。

examples.text: Anna sings the most beautifully in our class.
examples.zh: 安娜是我们班唱歌最好听的。

explain.zh: 讲过去的事，要交代「那时候正在……」，就用 was/were + 动词 -ing。它给故事铺背景，也常表示一个较长的动作被另一个动作打断，常和 when、while 连用。
explain.en: To say what was going on at a past moment, use was or were with the -ing form. It sets the scene and often shows a longer action that another action interrupts, usually with when or while.

form.zh: was/were + 动词-ing；was/were not + -ing
form.en: was/were + verb-ing; was/were not + verb-ing

pitfalls.zh: know、believe 这类状态动词不用进行时。
pitfalls.en: State verbs like know and believe are not used in the -ing form here.

pitfalls.zh: 只讲发生过什么事，用一般过去时，不用进行时。
pitfalls.en: For a single finished event, use the simple past, not the progressive.

examples.text: I was cooking when the phone rang.
examples.zh: 电话响的时候我正在做饭。

examples.text: At eight last night we were still waiting outside.
examples.zh: 昨晚八点我们还在外面等着。

explain.zh: 要说「到现在为止已经……」，用 have/has + 过去分词。它把过去的事和现在连起来：不点明具体时间，重点在结果还在，或者有没有这段经历。常和 just、already、yet、ever、never 一起用。
explain.en: Use have or has with the past participle for something up to now. It links the past to the present: no exact time is given, and the point is the result now, or whether the experience exists. It often goes with just, already, yet, ever and never.

form.zh: have/has + 过去分词；have not + 过去分词
form.en: have/has + past participle; have/has not + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 有明确的过去时间就用一般过去时：I saw him yesterday.
pitfalls.en: With a finished past time, use the simple past: I saw him yesterday.

pitfalls.zh: 第三人称单数用 has，其余用 have。
pitfalls.en: Use has with he, she and it; use have everywhere else.

pitfalls.zh: 不规则动词的过去分词要单独记：go 是 gone。
pitfalls.en: Learn irregular participles separately: go has gone, not went.

examples.text: I have just finished my homework.
examples.zh: 我刚做完作业。

examples.text: She has never been to Kyoto.
examples.zh: 她从没去过京都。

explain.zh: could 是 can 的过去式，也能单独用：讲过去会做的事、客气地提请求、说事情有可能。后面一律跟动词原形，不随人称变化。
explain.en: Could is the past form of can, and it also works on its own: for things you were able to do, for polite requests, and for what is possible. A base verb always follows, and the form never changes.

form.zh: could + 动词原形；could not（couldn't）
form.en: could + base verb; could not (couldn't)

pitfalls.zh: 后面跟动词原形，不加 to。
pitfalls.en: A base verb follows, with no to: not could to swim.

pitfalls.zh: 它没有第三人称变化：he could swim。
pitfalls.en: It never takes -s: he could swim, not he coulds swim.

examples.text: When I was six, I could swim well.
examples.zh: 我六岁时游泳游得很好。

examples.text: Could you open the window, please?
examples.zh: 你能把窗户打开吗？

explain.zh: 自己认定非做不可，或规定要求这么做，就用 must + 动词原形：You must wear a seat belt。语气很硬，也用来表示「事情准是这样」的推测。
explain.en: Use must with the base verb for something you feel is necessary, or that a rule requires: You must wear a seat belt. It is strong, and it also marks a confident guess about what is true.

form.zh: must + 动词原形；must not（mustn't）
form.en: must + base verb; must not (mustn't)

pitfalls.zh: mustn't 是禁止，不是不必；不必说 don't have to。
pitfalls.en: Mustn't means it is forbidden; for not necessary use don't have to.

pitfalls.zh: must 后接动词原形，不加 to，也不加 -s。
pitfalls.en: The verb after must is a base form: no to and no -s.

examples.text: You must show your ticket at the door.
examples.zh: 进门时必须出示门票。

examples.text: She must be tired after the trip.
examples.zh: 旅行之后她一定累了。

explain.zh: 觉得某件事是应该做的，用 should + 动词原形，比 must 软，是建议或提醒，不是命令。也可以说预期，指按理该发生的事。
explain.en: Use should with the base verb when you think something is the right thing to do. It is softer than must, so it gives advice or a reminder rather than an order. It can also say what you expect to happen.

form.zh: should + 动词原形；should not（shouldn't）
form.en: should + base verb; should not (shouldn't)

pitfalls.zh: 后面跟动词原形，不加 to，也不加 -s。
pitfalls.en: A base verb follows: not should to go, not should goes.

pitfalls.zh: 它只是建议，硬性规定要用 must。
pitfalls.en: It only advises; a strict rule that has to be obeyed takes must.

examples.text: You should drink more water.
examples.zh: 你应该多喝水。

examples.text: The train should arrive at nine.
examples.zh: 火车应该九点到。

explain.zh: 说主语「变得、感觉、看起来、听起来怎么样」，就在 become/feel/go/look/seem/sound 后面直接放形容词：She looks tired。形容词说的是主语的状态，不是动作怎么做，所以不用副词。
explain.en: To say how the subject becomes or seems, put an adjective straight after become, feel, go, look, seem or sound: She looks tired. The adjective describes the subject, not how the action is done, so no adverb is used.

form.zh: 主语 + become/feel/go/look/seem/sound + 形容词
form.en: subject + become/feel/go/look/seem/sound + adjective

pitfalls.zh: 后面用形容词：looks tired，不说 looks tiredly。
pitfalls.en: Use an adjective: looks tired, not looks tiredly.

pitfalls.zh: go 这样用时多指变坏：go bad、go wrong。
pitfalls.en: Go in this pattern usually means a change for the worse: go bad, go wrong.

examples.text: The room feels cold.
examples.zh: 这房间感觉有点冷。

examples.text: Your idea sounds great.
examples.zh: 你的主意听起来很棒。

name.zh: make + 宾语 + 形容词补语

explain.zh: 想说是谁或什么事让某人某物变成某个样子，用 make + 宾语 + 形容词：The news made her happy。形容词说的是宾语的状态，宾语后面不接 to be。
explain.en: Use make with an object and an adjective to say what causes someone or something to be a certain way: The news made her happy. The adjective describes the object, and no to be is needed after it.

form.zh: make + 宾语 + 形容词
form.en: make + object + adjective

pitfalls.zh: 宾语后直接放形容词，中间不加 to be。
pitfalls.en: The adjective follows the object directly: no to be in between.

pitfalls.zh: 别用副词代替形容词：made us happy，不说 made us happily。
pitfalls.en: Keep the adjective rather than an adverb: made us happy, not made us happily.

examples.text: The long walk made us tired.
examples.zh: 走了那么久，我们累了。

examples.text: Loud music makes me nervous.
examples.zh: 大声的音乐让我紧张。

explain.zh: 转述别人说过的话，用 tell + 人 + (that) 从句：She told me she was busy。tell 后面必须有人；转述时人称要换，动词常往过去退一步。
explain.en: To report what someone said, use tell, then the person, then a that-clause: She told me she was busy. Tell always needs the person. The pronouns shift, and the verb usually moves one step back into the past.

form.zh: tell + 人 + (that) + 从句
form.en: tell + person + (that) + clause

pitfalls.zh: tell 后面必须有人，不能说 tell that she was busy。
pitfalls.en: Tell needs a person: not tell that she was busy.

pitfalls.zh: 转述时别照抄原话的人称和时态。
pitfalls.en: Do not keep the original pronouns and tense when you report.

examples.text: He told me he would call later.
examples.zh: 他跟我说他晚点会打电话。

examples.text: My sister told us she had lost her keys.
examples.zh: 姐姐告诉我们她把钥匙丢了。

explain.zh: 把问题转述给别人，用 ask/remind/show/teach/tell + 人 + 疑问词 + 陈述语序：He asked me where I lived。疑问词后面的主语和动词不再颠倒，句末也不再用问号。
explain.en: To report a question, use ask, remind, show, teach or tell, then the person, then a question word and normal word order: He asked me where I lived. After the question word the subject and verb stay in statement order, and no question mark is used.

form.zh: ask/remind/show/teach/tell + 人 + 疑问词 + 陈述语序
form.en: ask/remind/show/teach/tell + person + question word + statement order

pitfalls.zh: 疑问词后面不要倒装：where I lived。
pitfalls.en: No inversion after the question word: where I lived, not where did I live.

pitfalls.zh: 整句是陈述，句末用句号，不用问号。
pitfalls.en: The whole sentence is a statement, so it ends with a full stop.

examples.text: She asked me what time the shop opened.
examples.zh: 她问我商店几点开门。

examples.text: Please show me how this machine works.
examples.zh: 请给我演示一下这台机器怎么用。

name.zh: 短语动词（动词 + 宾语 + 副词）

explain.zh: 动词后面加个 off、up 这样的副词，意思常常整个变掉，宾语可以放在它前面或后面：turn off the light 或 turn it off。宾语是代词时只能放中间：turn it off，不说 turn off it。
explain.en: A verb plus a small adverb like off or up often carries a whole new meaning, and the object can go before or after it: turn off the light or turn it off. When the object is a pronoun, it must go in the middle: turn it off, never turn off it.

form.zh: 动词 + 宾语 + 副词；代词宾语放中间
form.en: verb + object + adverb; a pronoun object goes in the middle

pitfalls.zh: 代词宾语只能放中间：pick it up。
pitfalls.en: A pronoun object goes in the middle: pick it up, not pick up it.

pitfalls.zh: 别按字面猜意思，look after 不是「往后看」。
pitfalls.en: Do not read the words literally: look after means take care of.

examples.text: Please turn the radio down.
examples.zh: 请把收音机声音调小。

examples.text: Can you look after my cat this weekend?
examples.zh: 这个周末你能帮我照看猫吗？

explain.zh: 要说「一个也没有」，就从 none of 起头，后面接出一个范围：none of the students、none of my friends。它等于 not any，回答 How many 或 Which 最常用。后面跟单数或复数动词都行，口语里复数更自然。
explain.en: Start with none of when you mean not one of a group: none of the students, none of my friends. It stands in for not any and is the usual answer to How many or Which. The verb after it can be singular or plural, and plural sounds more natural in speech.

form.zh: none of + the/my + 名词；动词单数复数皆可
form.en: none of + the/my + noun; singular or plural verb

pitfalls.zh: none 后面不能直接接名词，要说 none of them。
pitfalls.en: None cannot take a noun straight after it; say none of them.

pitfalls.zh: 问数量答 none，问 who 才用 no one。
pitfalls.en: Answer How many with none, and Who with no one.

examples.text: None of my friends likes football.
examples.zh: 我的朋友里没有一个喜欢足球。

examples.text: None of these keys opens the door.
examples.zh: 这些钥匙没有一把能开这扇门。

explain.zh: 想说「一个不错的什么东西」，形容词要放在 something 后面：something nice、nothing new。anything、everything 也一样，顺序是先 -thing 词，后形容词，不能倒过来说 nice something。
explain.en: When you mean a nice something, the adjective goes after the -thing word: something nice, nothing new. The same holds for anything and everything. The -thing word comes first, so nice something is not English.

form.zh: -thing 词在前 + 形容词
form.en: -thing word first, then the adjective

pitfalls.zh: 形容词别放前面：不说 a nice something。
pitfalls.en: Do not put the adjective first: a nice something is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 肯定句用 something，疑问和否定多用 anything。
pitfalls.en: Statements take something; questions and negatives usually take anything.

examples.text: I want something cold to drink.
examples.zh: 我想喝点凉的。

examples.text: There is nothing new in his story.
examples.zh: 他的故事里没有什么新东西。

explain.zh: 说两个人或两样东西一样，用 as + 形容词 + as：as tall as me。中间只放形容词或副词原形，不加 -er。想确认是不是一样，也可以直接问 Is it as big as that one?
explain.en: To say two people or things are the same, use as + adjective + as: as tall as me. Only the plain adjective or adverb goes in the middle, with no -er. To check whether they match, just ask Is it as big as that one?

form.zh: as + 形容词/副词原形 + as + 比较对象
form.en: as + adjective/adverb + as + the other thing

pitfalls.zh: 中间用原形，不说 as taller as。
pitfalls.en: Keep the plain form: as taller as is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 第二个 as 不能省：不说 as tall me。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop the second as: as tall me is wrong.

examples.text: My sister is as tall as my mother.
examples.zh: 我姐姐和我妈妈一样高。

examples.text: Is this box as heavy as that one?
examples.zh: 这个箱子和那个一样重吗？

name.zh: 否定同级比较：not as/so … as
name.en: COMPARISON OF EQUALITY: not as/so ... as

explain.zh: 说「甲不如乙」，用 not as + 形容词 + as：not as big as mine。口语里 not so … as 意思一样，书面稍多。它只是平实地比高低，比 than 的说法委婉。
explain.en: To say one thing falls short of another, use not as + adjective + as: not as big as mine. Spoken English also uses not so … as with the same meaning, and writing likes it a little more. It simply compares, and sounds softer than a than-clause.

form.zh: not as/so + 形容词/副词原形 + as + 比较对象
form.en: not as/so + adjective/adverb + as + the other thing

pitfalls.zh: 中间用原形，不说 not as bigger as。
pitfalls.en: Keep the plain form: not as bigger as is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 它表示「不如」，不是「不一样」。
pitfalls.en: It means less than, not simply different.

examples.text: This room is not as bright as the kitchen.
examples.zh: 这个房间不如厨房亮。

examples.text: The film was not so good as the book.
examples.zh: 这部电影不如书好看。

explain.zh: 说「看见、听见某人正在做什么」，在 see、watch、hear 后面先放人，再放 -ing：I saw him running。keep 也一样，表示让某事一直持续。这里说的是动作正在进行，而不是做完了。
explain.en: When you see or hear someone in the middle of doing something, put the person first and the -ing form after see, watch or hear: I saw him running. Keep works the same way for something that goes on. The point is an action in progress, not one already finished.

form.zh: see/watch/hear/keep + 宾语 + 动词 -ing
form.en: see/watch/hear/keep + object + -ing form

pitfalls.zh: 后面不加 to：不说 I saw him to run。
pitfalls.en: No to here: I saw him to run is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 说做完的整件事，用动词原形不用 -ing。
pitfalls.en: For a whole finished action, use the base verb, not -ing.

examples.text: I saw her waiting at the bus stop.
examples.zh: 我看见她在公交站等车。

examples.text: Keep the water running for a minute.
examples.zh: 让水先流一分钟。

explain.zh: 说「需要做某事」，用 need to + 动词原形：I need to go。它也可以直接带名词：I need a pen。否定 don't need to 是「不必」，语气比 must 的否定轻得多。
explain.en: Say need to + a base verb when something has to be done: I need to go. Need can also take a noun by itself: I need a pen. The negative don't need to means it is not necessary, which is much softer than must not.

form.zh: need to + 动词原形；need + 名词；don't need to
form.en: need to + base verb; need + noun; don't need to

pitfalls.zh: need to 后接原形，不说 need to going。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb after need to, not an -ing form.

pitfalls.zh: don't need to 是「不必」，不是「不准」。
pitfalls.en: Don't need to means it is not necessary, not that it is forbidden.

examples.text: You need to show your ticket at the door.
examples.zh: 你需要在门口出示车票。

examples.text: We don't need to hurry.
examples.zh: 我们不用赶时间。

explain.zh: 想请对方进来坐坐、一起吃点东西，用 Won't you + 动词原形起头，比 Would you like 更热络：Won't you come in? 它外形是否定问句，意思是「要不要……」。答语说 Yes, I'd love to.
explain.en: Use Won't you + a base verb to invite someone in or offer them something, warmer than Would you like: Won't you come in? It looks like a negative question but means would you like to. A natural answer is Yes, I'd love to.

form.zh: Won't you + 动词原形？
form.en: Won't you + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: 它是在邀请，别当成真的否定问句。
pitfalls.en: It is an invitation, not a real negative question.

pitfalls.zh: 后接动词原形，不说 Won't you to come。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb: Won't you to come is wrong.

examples.text: Won't you sit down and have some tea?
examples.zh: 坐下来喝杯茶吧？

examples.text: Won't you join us for dinner?
examples.zh: 要不要来和我们一起吃晚饭？

explain.zh: 看见别人需要帮忙，主动开口，用 Shall I + 动词原形：Shall I carry it? 意思是「我来……好吗」。答语常是 Yes, please. 或 No, thanks.
explain.en: When you see that someone needs a hand, offer it with Shall I + a base verb: Shall I carry it? The meaning is let me do that for you. People answer Yes, please. or No, thanks.

form.zh: Shall I + 动词原形？
form.en: Shall I + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: 要主动去做的人是自己，别用 Shall you。
pitfalls.en: The offer is about yourself, so never Shall you.

pitfalls.zh: 后接原形，不说 Shall I to help。
pitfalls.en: The base verb follows: Shall I to help is wrong.

examples.text: Shall I carry your bag?
examples.zh: 要我帮你拿包吗？

examples.text: Shall I call a taxi?
examples.zh: 我叫辆出租车好吗？

explain.zh: 提议一起做某事，用 Shall we + 动词原形：Shall we start? 主语是 we，把听话的人也算进去，比 Let's 更像在征询意见。
explain.en: Use Shall we + a base verb to suggest doing something together: Shall we start? The subject is we, so the other person is included, and it asks for agreement more openly than Let's.

form.zh: Shall we + 动词原形？
form.en: Shall we + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: 后接原形，不说 Shall we starting。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb: Shall we starting is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 它是在问对方意见，不是替对方决定。
pitfalls.en: It asks what the other person thinks; it does not decide for them.

examples.text: Shall we start the meeting now?
examples.zh: 我们现在开始开会好吗？

examples.text: Shall we walk to the station?
examples.zh: 我们走去车站好吗？

explain.zh: 拿不定主意、想听别人意见，用 Should I + 动词原形：Should I tell her? 意思是「我该不该……」。回答常用 Yes, you should. 或 No, you shouldn't.
explain.en: When you cannot decide and want advice, ask Should I + a base verb: Should I tell her? It means would it be right for me to. The usual answers are Yes, you should. and No, you shouldn't.

form.zh: Should I + 动词原形？
form.en: Should I + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: 这是问自己该不该，不是请别人去做。
pitfalls.en: It asks about your own next move, not someone else's action.

pitfalls.zh: 后接原形，不说 Should I to go。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb: Should I to go is wrong.

examples.text: Should I tell her the news today?
examples.zh: 我今天该把消息告诉她吗？

examples.text: Should I take an umbrella?
examples.zh: 我该带把伞吗？

explain.zh: 说「有能力做某事」，除了 can，还可以用 be able to + 动词原形：I was able to finish it。can 没有将来式和完成式，需要这些说法时就换成 be able to。
explain.en: Besides can, you can say be able to + a base verb for something you have the ability to do: I was able to finish it. Can has no future or perfect form, so be able to takes over when you need one.

form.zh: be able to + 动词原形；否定 be not able to
form.en: be able to + base verb; negative be not able to

pitfalls.zh: to 后面接原形，不说 able to doing。
pitfalls.en: After to use the base verb: able to doing is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: able 前要有 be：不说 I able to swim。
pitfalls.en: Keep the be: I able to swim is wrong.

examples.text: She was able to solve the problem alone.
examples.zh: 她一个人就把问题解决了。

examples.text: Will you be able to come tomorrow?
examples.zh: 你明天能来吗？

explain.zh: 觉得某事也许会发生，但把握不大，用 might + 动词原形：It might rain。它比 may 更不确定，也更口语。might 不随人称变化，后面也不加 to。
explain.en: Use might + a base verb when something may happen but you are not sure: It might rain. It is less certain and more conversational than may. Might never changes for person, and no to comes after it.

form.zh: might + 动词原形；否定 might not
form.en: might + base verb; negative might not

pitfalls.zh: 后接原形，不说 might to rain 或 might rains。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb: might to rain and might rains are both wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 它只说「也许」，不表示许可。
pitfalls.en: It only says maybe; it does not give permission.

examples.text: Take a coat; it might be cold tonight.
examples.zh: 带件外套吧，今晚可能冷。

examples.text: She might not come to the party.
examples.zh: 她也许不会来参加聚会。

explain.zh: 猜某人此刻或最近正在做什么，用 may/might/could/must + be + -ing：He must be sleeping。它把「也许、一定」和「正在」合在一起，说的是眼前正在发生的事。
explain.en: To guess what someone is doing right now, use may, might, could or must + be + -ing: He must be sleeping. It joins a judgement like maybe or surely to an action in progress, so it is about what is going on at this moment.

form.zh: 情态动词 + be + 动词 -ing
form.en: modal + be + -ing form

pitfalls.zh: be 不能省：不说 He must sleeping。
pitfalls.en: Keep the be: He must sleeping is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 这里说正在发生，说完的事用 have done。
pitfalls.en: This is about now; for a finished action use have done.

examples.text: The lights are on; they must be working late.
examples.zh: 灯还亮着，他们一定在加班。

examples.text: She might be waiting for us outside.
examples.zh: 她也许正在外面等我们。

explain.zh: 想说「将会有…」「可能会有…」，就在 there 后面先放助动词，再接 be。它讲的还是某处有某物，只是添上将来、猜测或允许的意思。否定把 not 加在助动词上，疑问把助动词提到 there 前面。
explain.en: When you want to say that something will, may or must exist somewhere, put an auxiliary after there and before be. The sentence still says that something exists, with an added idea of future, possibility or permission. Negatives put not on the auxiliary, and questions move the auxiliary in front of there.

form.zh: there + 助动词（will/can/must）+ be；否定 there + 助动词 + not + be
form.en: there + auxiliary (will/can/must) + be; negative there + auxiliary + not + be

pitfalls.zh: 助动词别放到 there 前面：不说 Will be there a party。
pitfalls.en: Do not put the auxiliary before there: Will be there a party is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 助动词后只接 be 的原形：不说 there will is。
pitfalls.en: Only the base form be follows the auxiliary: there will is is wrong.

examples.text: There will be a test next Monday.
examples.zh: 下周一有一场考试。

examples.text: Will there be enough chairs for everyone?
examples.zh: 椅子够所有人坐吗？

explain.zh: 碰上不知道、想弄清楚的事，把 what、where、when、who、why、how 这类词放在 know 或 wonder 后面，让它带出一个小句子。这个小句子用陈述词序，主语在动词前面，不摆成问句的样子。
explain.en: When you do not know something and want to talk about it, put a wh- word such as what, where, when, who or how after know or wonder and let it begin a short clause. That clause keeps statement order, with the subject before the verb, so it does not look like a question.

form.zh: know / wonder + what/where/when/who/why/how + 主语 + 动词
form.en: know / wonder + what/where/when/who/why/how + subject + verb

pitfalls.zh: 从句里别倒装：不说 I wonder where is he。
pitfalls.en: Keep statement order in the clause: I wonder where is he is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 也别借用 do/does 提问：不说 Do you know where does she live?
pitfalls.en: Do not build the clause like a question with do: Do you know where does she live? is wrong.

examples.text: I don't know where my keys are.
examples.zh: 我不知道我的钥匙在哪儿。

examples.text: She wondered why the shop was closed.
examples.zh: 她想知道那家店为什么关门了。

explain.zh: 两件事紧挨着发生，用 as soon as 接住先发生的那件，说「一…就…」。它后面跟一个完整小句子，主句讲紧接着发生的事。讲过去的事，从句和主句都用过去时。
explain.en: Use as soon as when two things happen one right after the other; the clause after it names the first event, and the main clause names what follows. A full clause follows as soon as. For past events, both the clause and the main clause take a past tense.

form.zh: as soon as + 主语 + 谓语，主句讲后发生的事
form.en: as soon as + subject + verb, then the main clause

pitfalls.zh: 讲将来的事，从句用一般现在时：不说 as soon as he will come。
pitfalls.en: For future events use the present tense in the clause: as soon as he will come is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: as soon as 后面要接完整小句子，不能只接名词。
pitfalls.en: A full clause must follow as soon as, not just a noun.

examples.text: As soon as I got home, it started to rain.
examples.zh: 我一到家就下起雨来。

examples.text: Call me as soon as you arrive.
examples.zh: 你一到就给我打电话。

explain.zh: 请人做事或吩咐人做事，用 ask/tell + 某人 + to do。ask 是请求，语气客气；tell 是吩咐，语气直接。要说不许做，就把 not 放在 to 前面。
explain.en: Use ask or tell + a person + to do when you want someone to do something. Ask makes a polite request, while tell gives a direct instruction. For the negative, put not before to.

form.zh: ask / tell + 人 + to + 动词原形；否定 not to do
form.en: ask / tell + person + to + base verb; negative not to do

pitfalls.zh: to 不能省：不说 ask someone do。
pitfalls.en: Keep to: ask someone do is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 否定别用 don't：不说 tell him don't go。
pitfalls.en: Do not use don't: tell him don't go is wrong.

examples.text: She asked me to close the door.
examples.zh: 她请我把门关上。

examples.text: The teacher told us not to talk in class.
examples.zh: 老师让我们上课别讲话。

name.zh: for + 名词 + to do（不定式的逻辑主语）

explain.zh: 要说「某人做某事」怎么样，用 for + 某人 + to do 把做事的人点出来。这个 for 短语常跟在形容词或名词后面，说明这件事轮到谁做。
explain.en: When you need to name the person who does the action, use for + person + to do. This for phrase often follows an adjective or a noun and makes clear who is meant to do the action.

form.zh: for + 名词 / 代词宾格 + to + 动词原形
form.en: for + noun or object pronoun + to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: for 后用宾格：说 for him to go，不说 for he。
pitfalls.en: Use the object pronoun after for: for him to go, not for he.

pitfalls.zh: for 不能省：不说 It is hard me to decide。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop for: It is hard me to decide is wrong.

examples.text: It is hard for him to get up early.
examples.zh: 对他来说，早起很难。

examples.text: There is no need for us to hurry.
examples.zh: 我们没必要着急。

explain.zh: shall 跟在 I 或 we 后面，用来问对方意见、提建议，最常见的是 Shall we…? 它也见于规定和承诺，多出现在正式文件和较老的英语里。
explain.en: Shall follows I or we to ask for someone's opinion or to make a suggestion, most often in Shall we…? It also appears in rules and promises, mostly in formal documents and older English.

form.zh: shall + 动词原形；疑问 Shall I / we + 动词原形？
form.en: shall + base verb; question Shall I / we + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: shall 后接动词原形，不加 to，也不加 -s。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb after shall: no to, no -s.

pitfalls.zh: 日常提建议口语多说 Should we…?，shall 偏正式。
pitfalls.en: In everyday speech Should we…? is more common; shall sounds formal.

examples.text: Shall we meet at six?
examples.zh: 我们六点见面好吗？

examples.text: Shall I open the window for you?
examples.zh: 我帮你把窗户打开好吗？

explain.zh: 问「和谁」「用哪个」这类事，把介词提到疑问词前面：With whom…? In which…? 这种说法正式、偏书面。日常口语更常把介词留在句子末尾。
explain.en: To ask questions such as 'with whom' or 'in which', move the preposition in front of the wh- word: With whom…? In which…? This order is formal and mostly written. In everyday speech the preposition usually stays at the end.

form.zh: 介词 + what/which/whom/whose + 助动词 + 主语 + 动词？
form.en: preposition + what/which/whom/whose + auxiliary + subject + verb?

pitfalls.zh: 介词已提前，句末不再重复：不说 With whom did you go with?
pitfalls.en: Do not repeat the preposition at the end: With whom did you go with? is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 介词后指人用 whom，不用 who。
pitfalls.en: After a preposition use whom, not who.

examples.text: With whom did you go to the concert?
examples.zh: 你和谁一起去的音乐会？

examples.text: In which drawer did you put the keys?
examples.zh: 你把钥匙放进哪个抽屉了？

explain.zh: 要讲将来某个时刻正干着什么，用 will be + 动词 -ing。它不带「打算」的意思，只把那一刻的画面说成正在进行。问别人的安排时用它，也比直接问计划客气。
explain.en: Use will be + verb-ing to say what will be going on at a point in the future. It carries no idea of intention; it simply pictures the action in progress at that moment. Asking about someone's arrangements this way also sounds more polite than asking about plans directly.

form.zh: will be + 动词 -ing；否定 will not be doing；疑问 Will you be doing…?
form.en: will be + verb-ing; negative will not be doing; question Will you be doing…?

pitfalls.zh: be 不能漏：不说 I will working at nine。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop be: I will working at nine is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 讲打算做什么用它不对，那是 will do 或 be going to do。
pitfalls.en: It does not express a plan; for plans use will do or be going to do.

examples.text: This time tomorrow I will be flying to Tokyo.
examples.zh: 明天这个时候，我正飞往东京。

examples.text: Will you be using the car this evening?
examples.zh: 今晚你要用车吗？

explain.zh: 想说说话人对整件事的看法，用 fortunately、clearly、apparently 这类副词，多数放在句首，后面加个逗号。它评的是整句话，不是某一个动作。
explain.en: Use an adverb such as fortunately, clearly or apparently to show the speaker's view of the whole statement. Most of them go at the start of the sentence, followed by a comma. They comment on the whole sentence, not on a single action.

form.zh: 副词 + 逗号 + 整句；也可插在句中
form.en: adverb + comma + the whole sentence; it can also stand mid-sentence

pitfalls.zh: 别用形容词形：说 Fortunately, we won，不说 Fortunate。
pitfalls.en: Do not use the adjective form: Fortunately, we won, not Fortunate.

pitfalls.zh: 放句首时后面要加逗号，别和整句连成一串。
pitfalls.en: Put a comma after a sentence-initial adverb.

examples.text: Unfortunately, the train was late again.
examples.zh: 不幸的是，火车又晚点了。

examples.text: Apparently, she has moved to another city.
examples.zh: 看样子她搬到另一个城市去了。

explain.zh: 先行词是人，而这个人在后面的小句里当宾语，就用 who 引出：the man who I met。who 提到前面，小句仍按陈述词序排，不倒装。
explain.en: When the noun before the clause is a person and that person is the object inside the clause, use who: the man who I met. Who moves to the front, but the clause keeps statement order and does not invert.

form.zh: 名词（人）+ who + 主语 + 动词
form.en: person + who + subject + verb

pitfalls.zh: who 后面别倒装：不说 the man who did I meet。
pitfalls.en: Keep statement order after who: the man who did I meet is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 指人别用 which，which 只指物。
pitfalls.en: Do not use which for a person; which refers to things.

examples.text: The woman who we saw at the station was my aunt.
examples.zh: 我们在车站看到的那个女人是我姑妈。

examples.text: He is a friend who everyone likes.
examples.zh: 他是个大家都喜欢的朋友。

explain.zh: 先行词是人、在后面的小句里当宾语时，正式的说法用 whom 引出：the man whom I met。它比 who 更书面，口语里常换成 who，或者干脆省掉。
explain.en: When the person before the clause is the object inside it, formal English uses whom: the man whom I met. It is more written than who; in speech people often use who instead, or leave the word out.

form.zh: 名词（人）+ whom + 主语 + 动词
form.en: person + whom + subject + verb

pitfalls.zh: whom 只当宾语，不能作主语：不说 the man whom called me。
pitfalls.en: Whom is only an object: the man whom called me is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: whom 后面不倒装，也不加 do。
pitfalls.en: No inversion and no do after whom.

examples.text: The doctor whom she consulted was very kind.
examples.zh: 她咨询的那位医生非常和善。

examples.text: This is the writer whom I admire most.
examples.zh: 这是我最敬佩的作家。

explain.zh: 先行词是物或事情，而它在后面的小句里当宾语，就用 which 引出：the book which I bought。which 占的是宾语的位置，小句照样按陈述词序排。
explain.en: When the noun before the clause is a thing and it is the object inside the clause, use which: the book which I bought. Which fills the object slot, and the clause still keeps statement order.

form.zh: 名词（物）+ which + 主语 + 动词
form.en: thing + which + subject + verb

pitfalls.zh: 宾语别重复：不说 the book which I bought it。
pitfalls.en: Do not repeat the object: the book which I bought it is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: which 不指人，指人要用 who 或 whom。
pitfalls.en: Which is not for people; use who or whom.

examples.text: This is the camera which he used last year.
examples.zh: 这就是他去年用的那台相机。

examples.text: The song which they played was my favourite.
examples.zh: 他们放的那首歌是我的最爱。

explain.zh: 先行词是人或物，而它在后面的小句里当宾语，可以用 that 引出：the book that I bought、the man that I met。that 在口语里最常见，也常整个省掉。
explain.en: When the noun before the clause, person or thing, is the object inside it, that can introduce the clause: the book that I bought, the man that I met. That is the most common choice in speech, and it is often left out altogether.

form.zh: 名词 + that + 主语 + 动词；that 可省略
form.en: noun + that + subject + verb; that can be omitted

pitfalls.zh: 宾语别重复：不说 the film that I saw it。
pitfalls.en: Do not repeat the object: the film that I saw it is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: that 不能直接跟在介词后：不说 the man with that I talked。
pitfalls.en: That cannot follow a preposition: the man with that I talked is wrong.

examples.text: The film that we watched last night was boring.
examples.zh: 我们昨晚看的那部电影很无聊。

examples.text: She is the teacher that I told you about.
examples.zh: 她就是我跟你说过的那位老师。

explain.zh: 说两个人互相做同一件事，就在动词后面加 each other。主语必须有两个以上的人或物，each other 只能作宾语，不能当主语用。
explain.en: Use each other after a verb when two or more people do the same thing to one another. The subject must cover two or more people or things, and each other works as an object, never as the subject.

form.zh: each other 作宾语；所有格 each other's
form.en: each other as object; possessive each other's

pitfalls.zh: 主语得是两个以上的人或物，一个人不能用。
pitfalls.en: The subject needs two or more people or things; one person cannot use it.

pitfalls.zh: 「互相」别用 themselves：They like themselves 是各自喜欢自己。
pitfalls.en: Do not use themselves for 'each other': They like themselves means each one likes himself or herself.

examples.text: The two sisters write to each other every week.
examples.zh: 两姐妹每周互相写信。

examples.text: Tom and I help each other with homework.
examples.zh: 汤姆和我互相帮忙做作业。

explain.zh: 笼统说「还有一些别的」，用 others，后面不接名词。它指没说清的另一部分人，不能指剩下的全部；剩下的全部用 the others。
explain.en: Use others on its own to mean 'some other people or things' without naming them. No noun follows it. It does not mean all the rest; for that, use the others.

form.zh: others 单独用，后面不接名词
form.en: others on its own, with no noun after it

pitfalls.zh: others 后面不能再跟名词：不说 others people。
pitfalls.en: No noun can follow others: not others people.

pitfalls.zh: 指剩下的全部要用 the others，不用 others。
pitfalls.en: For all the remaining ones, use the others, not others.

examples.text: Some people like tea; others prefer coffee.
examples.zh: 有些人喜欢茶，另一些人更喜欢咖啡。

examples.text: Be kind to others.
examples.zh: 对别人要友善。

explain.zh: 说「太……做不了」，用 too + 形容词/副词 + to do。程度过头，结果就是做不到；to 后面直接跟动词原形，不用再加 not。
explain.en: When a degree is so high that the action cannot happen, use too + adjective/adverb + to + base verb. The first part gives the extreme degree, and the to-infinitive names the action that becomes impossible.

form.zh: too + 形/副 + (for sb) + to do
form.en: too + adjective/adverb + (for somebody) + to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: to 不定式已含否定，不要再加 not。
pitfalls.en: The to-infinitive already carries the negative idea; do not add not.

pitfalls.zh: 别用 very 代替 too：very tired to walk 不成立。
pitfalls.en: Do not use very here: very tired to walk is wrong.

examples.text: He was too young to drive the truck.
examples.zh: 他太小，开不了那辆卡车。

examples.text: This box is too heavy to carry alone.
examples.zh: 这箱子太重，一个人搬不动。

name.zh: so + 形容词/副词 + that 从句

explain.zh: 说「如此……以至于」，用 so + 形容词/副词 + that 接一个从句。前半句给出程度，that 后面写因此发生的结果；口语里 that 常常省掉。
explain.en: Use so + adjective/adverb + that + clause to say that a degree produces a result. The first half gives the degree, and the that-clause tells what happens because of it. In speech that is often left out.

form.zh: so + 形/副 + that 从句
form.en: so + adjective/adverb + that + clause

pitfalls.zh: so 后面只放形容词或副词，不放名词。
pitfalls.en: Only an adjective or adverb follows so, never a noun.

pitfalls.zh: that 后面必须是完整句子。
pitfalls.en: A full clause must follow that.

examples.text: The room was so dark that we could not see the door.
examples.zh: 房间太暗，我们看不见门。

examples.text: She spoke so quickly that nobody understood her.
examples.zh: 她说得太快，没人听懂。

name.zh: 比较级 + and + 比较级

explain.zh: 说一件事不断变得更怎么样，就把同一个比较级用 and 连起来：bigger and bigger。多音节词说 more and more + 原级，前后两半用同一个词。
explain.en: To say something keeps changing in the same direction, repeat the same comparative and join the two with and: bigger and bigger. With longer adjectives, use more and more + base form.

form.zh: 比较级 + and + 比较级；多音节用 more and more + 原级
form.en: comparative + and + comparative; longer words take more and more + base form

pitfalls.zh: 多音节用 more and more，不写 more colder。
pitfalls.en: Longer words take more and more; do not write more colder.

pitfalls.zh: and 两边用同一个词：more and more cars。
pitfalls.en: Keep the same word on both sides: more and more cars.

examples.text: The noise outside grew louder and louder.
examples.zh: 外面的声音越来越大。

examples.text: More and more people are working from home.
examples.zh: 越来越多的人在家工作。

explain.zh: 差距比一般比较级更大时，在比较级前加 even、much、far、a lot 或 still。even 带点出乎意料，still 常说「还要更」；very 不能这样用。
explain.en: Put even, much, far, a lot or still before a comparative to make the difference larger. Even often adds surprise, and still usually means 'even more so'. These words strengthen the comparison without changing its form.

form.zh: even/much/far/a lot/still + 比较级
form.en: even / much / far / a lot / still + comparative

pitfalls.zh: 不用 very 修饰比较级：不说 very bigger。
pitfalls.en: Do not use very with a comparative: not very bigger.

pitfalls.zh: 比较级本身已含比较，别再加 more：不说 more better。
pitfalls.en: The comparative already compares; do not add more: not more better.

examples.text: This bag is much heavier than mine.
examples.zh: 这个包比我的重得多。

examples.text: The second test was even harder.
examples.zh: 第二次测验甚至更难。

explain.zh: 叫人保持某种状态，就用 Be + 形容词开头，主语不写出来。小心、安静、准时这类提醒都常用；否定形式是 Don't be…。
explain.en: To tell someone to be in a certain state, start with Be + adjective and leave the subject out. It suits reminders like being careful, quiet or on time. The negative is Don't be + adjective.

form.zh: Be + 形容词；否定 Don't be + 形容词
form.en: Be + adjective; negative Don't be + adjective

pitfalls.zh: 别加主语 you，也别加 to：Be careful.
pitfalls.en: Leave out you and to: Be careful.

pitfalls.zh: be 不能换成 is/are：不说 Is careful.
pitfalls.en: Keep be in the base form: not Is careful.

examples.text: Be careful with that glass.
examples.zh: 小心那个玻璃杯。

examples.text: Don't be late for the meeting.
examples.zh: 开会别迟到。

explain.zh: 说「不得不、必须」，用 have got to + 动词原形，意思和 must 接近。口语里很常用，尤其在英式英语里；主语是 he/she 时换成 has got to。
explain.en: Use have got to + base verb to say that something has to be done, close in meaning to must. It is common in speech, especially in British English. With he, she or it, use has got to.

form.zh: have/has got to + 动词原形
form.en: have/has got to + base verb; negative haven't/hasn't got to

pitfalls.zh: got 后面必须带 to：不说 I have got go.
pitfalls.en: got must be followed by to: not I have got go.

pitfalls.zh: 主语是 he/she 时用 has got to。
pitfalls.en: With he, she or it, use has got to.

examples.text: I have got to finish this report tonight.
examples.zh: 我今晚必须写完这份报告。

examples.text: She has got to see the doctor.
examples.zh: 她得去看医生。

explain.zh: 请求允许或说某事有可能，用 may + 动词原形。求许可时比 can 客气、正式，说可能性时意思是「也许」；否定用 may not。
explain.en: Use may + base verb to ask for permission or to say that something is possible. For permission it sounds more formal and polite than can; for possibility it means 'perhaps'. The negative is may not.

form.zh: may + 动词原形；否定 may not
form.en: may + base verb; negative may not

pitfalls.zh: may 后跟原形，不加 -s 或 to：不说 may goes.
pitfalls.en: The base verb follows may, with no -s and no to: not may goes.

pitfalls.zh: may not 多表示「不可以」，别读成「不可能」。
pitfalls.en: may not usually means 'is not allowed', not 'is impossible'.

examples.text: May I use your phone for a minute?
examples.zh: 我能借用一下你的手机吗？

examples.text: It may rain this afternoon.
examples.zh: 今天下午可能会下雨。

explain.zh: 说「按理应该」，用 ought to + 动词原形，语气接近 should。多指按道理、规矩或义务该做的事；否定是 ought not to。
explain.en: Use ought to + base verb to say what is right, expected or a duty, close in meaning to should. It often points to rules or to what is reasonable. The negative is ought not to.

form.zh: ought to + 动词原形；否定 ought not to
form.en: ought to + base verb; negative ought not to

pitfalls.zh: ought 后面必须带 to：不说 You ought go.
pitfalls.en: ought must be followed by to: not You ought go.

pitfalls.zh: 否定写 ought not to，不用 don't ought。
pitfalls.en: The negative is ought not to, never don't ought.

examples.text: You ought to apologize to her.
examples.zh: 你应该向她道歉。

examples.text: We ought to leave before it gets dark.
examples.zh: 我们应该在天黑前出发。

explain.zh: 说过去常做、现在不做了，用 used to + 动词原形。也可以说过去的状态，比如以前住在哪里；句子只讲过去，和现在对照。
explain.en: Use used to + base verb for something you often did in the past but do not do now. It also describes a past state that has changed, such as where you lived. The sentence looks only at the past and contrasts it with the present.

form.zh: used to + 动词原形；否定 didn't use to
form.en: used to + base verb; negative didn't use to; question Did … use to …?

pitfalls.zh: used to 后面跟动词原形，不跟 -ing。
pitfalls.en: A base verb follows used to, not an -ing form.

pitfalls.zh: be used to doing 是「习惯于」，别混用。
pitfalls.en: be used to doing means 'be accustomed to'; keep the two patterns apart.

examples.text: My grandfather used to work in a factory.
examples.zh: 我爷爷以前在工厂工作。

examples.text: There used to be a small shop on this corner.
examples.zh: 这个街角以前有家小店。

explain.zh: 说「已经有、一直存在」，用 There has/have been + 名词。讲从过去到现在这段时间里发生或存在的事，后面常接数量或时间段；单数用 has been，复数用 have been。
explain.en: Use There has/have been + noun to say that something has existed or happened up to now. It covers the stretch of time from the past to the present and often comes with a number or a period. Use has been for one thing and have been for several.

form.zh: There has/have been + 名词
form.en: There has/have been + noun; has for one thing, have for several

pitfalls.zh: 看后面的名词定 has 还是 have：two calls 用 have been。
pitfalls.en: The noun decides has or have: two calls take have been.

pitfalls.zh: been 不能换成 be：不说 There has be…
pitfalls.en: Keep been: not There has be an accident.

examples.text: There has been a lot of rain this week.
examples.zh: 这周雨下得很多。

examples.text: There have been three calls for you this morning.
examples.zh: 今天上午有三个电话找你。

name.zh: 目的状语从句 so that

explain.zh: 说「为了……」，用 so that 接一个从句：前面写做法，后面写想达到的结果，从句里常带 can、could 或 will。口语里 that 有时省略。
explain.en: Use so that + clause to give the purpose of an action. The first part says what is done, and the clause says the result you want, often with can, could or will. In speech that is sometimes dropped.

form.zh: so that + 从句（常含 can/could）
form.en: so that + clause, often with can, could or will

pitfalls.zh: so that 后面要接完整句子，不能只接名词。
pitfalls.en: A full clause follows so that, not a bare noun.

pitfalls.zh: 表目的用 so that，别与结果句 so…that 混用。
pitfalls.en: so that gives a purpose; so … that gives a result.

examples.text: She spoke slowly so that everyone could follow her.
examples.zh: 她讲得很慢，好让大家都跟得上。

examples.text: I left early so that I could catch the bus.
examples.zh: 我早早出门，好赶上公交车。

name.zh: 形式主语 it + be + 形容词 + that 从句

explain.zh: 说「……是清楚的／重要的是」，用 It is + 形容词 + that 从句。it 只是占位，真正的内容在 that 后面；把评论放前面，句子更好读。
explain.en: Use It is + adjective + that + clause to comment on a fact. The it is only a placeholder, and the real content comes after that. Putting the comment first makes a long sentence easier to read.

form.zh: It is/was + 形容词 + that 从句
form.en: It is/was + adjective + that + clause

pitfalls.zh: that 后面要是完整句子，别只接名词。
pitfalls.en: A full clause follows that, not a bare noun.

pitfalls.zh: 句首的 it 不能换成 this 或 that。
pitfalls.en: The opening it cannot be replaced by this or that.

examples.text: It is clear that she needs more time.
examples.zh: 很明显她需要更多时间。

examples.text: It was strange that nobody noticed the noise.
examples.zh: 奇怪的是没人注意到那声音。

explain.zh: 补充说明一个人或东西，用逗号隔开 who/which 从句。去掉从句主句照样成立，它只是多给信息；指人用 who，指物用 which，不用 that。
explain.en: Use a comma plus who or which to add extra information about a person or thing. The main sentence still stands without the clause, which only gives more detail. Use who for people, which for things, and never that.

form.zh: 名词, who/which + 从句（逗号隔开）
form.en: noun, who/which + clause, set off by commas

pitfalls.zh: 补充说明的从句不用 that，逗号也不能省。
pitfalls.en: That cannot be used here, and the commas cannot be dropped.

pitfalls.zh: 从句只管补充信息，不限定是哪一个。
pitfalls.en: The clause adds information; it does not single out which one.

examples.text: My uncle, who lives in Canada, is visiting us.
examples.zh: 我叔叔住在加拿大，他正来看我们。

examples.text: The old bridge, which was built in 1900, is still in use.
examples.zh: 那座老桥建于一九〇〇年，现在仍在使用。

explain.zh: 介词提到关系代词前面，写成「介词 + which/whom」。多为正式书面语；指物用 which，指人用 whom，介词后面不能用 that。
explain.en: Move the preposition in front of the relative pronoun: preposition + which or whom. This belongs to formal, mostly written English. Use which for things and whom for people; that cannot follow a preposition.

form.zh: 介词 + which/whom + 从句
form.en: preposition + which/whom + clause

pitfalls.zh: 介词后面不能用 that 或 who。
pitfalls.en: That and who cannot follow the preposition.

pitfalls.zh: 口语里介词常留句末：the house he lived in。
pitfalls.en: In speech the preposition often stays at the end: the house he lived in.

examples.text: The room in which we met was very quiet.
examples.zh: 我们见面的那个房间很安静。

examples.text: She is the teacher from whom I learned most.
examples.zh: 她是我受益最多的那位老师。

explain.zh: 说「这就是……的地方／时候」，where 或 when 直接接在 This is、That was 后面，前面不加名词。它已经含了「地方」「时候」的意思，后面跟一个完整句子。
explain.en: Use where or when straight after This is or That was, with no noun in front of it. The adverb already carries the idea of place or time, and a full clause follows. It answers the question 'which place?' or 'which time?'.

form.zh: This is/That was + where/when + 从句
form.en: This is / That was + where or when + clause

pitfalls.zh: where/when 前不加名词，直接接在 is/was 后。
pitfalls.en: No noun comes before where or when; they follow is or was directly.

pitfalls.zh: 别用 which 代替：不说 This is which he lives.
pitfalls.en: Do not use which instead: not This is which he lives.

examples.text: This is where the old market used to be.
examples.zh: 这里就是老市场原来的地方。

examples.text: That was when everything changed.
examples.zh: 就是那时候一切变了。

explain.zh: 用逗号加 when/where 从句，给时间或地点补充说明。前面已有明确的时间或地点名词，从句只是附加信息，去掉也成立；不能用 that 代替。
explain.en: Use a comma plus when or where to add a comment about a time or place. The noun before it already names the time or place, and the clause only adds detail, so the sentence stands without it. That cannot be used instead.

form.zh: 时间/地点名词, when/where + 从句
form.en: time or place noun, when/where + clause, with a comma

pitfalls.zh: 补充说明的从句前，逗号不能省。
pitfalls.en: The comma before the added clause cannot be dropped.

pitfalls.zh: 别用 that 代替 when/where。
pitfalls.en: That cannot replace when or where here.

examples.text: We moved to Beijing in 2010, when my son was born.
examples.zh: 我们二〇一〇年搬到北京，那年我儿子出生。

examples.text: They visited the village, where his mother grew up.
examples.zh: 他们去了那个村子，他母亲在那里长大。

name.zh: 介词留在句尾的关系从句

explain.zh: 想留住句尾的介词，就看从句里缺了哪个宾语。关系从句用 who、that 或干脆省略，介词一动不动留在最后：the book I told you about。这样比把介词提到前面口语得多，日常对话几乎都这么说。
explain.en: To keep the preposition at the end, look at what the clause is missing. In a relative clause you use who or that, or leave the word out altogether, and the preposition stays where it is: the book I told you about. This is far more natural in speech than moving the preposition forward, and conversation almost always does it this way.

form.zh: 名词 + (that/who) + 从句 + 介词；关系词可省略
form.en: noun + (that/who) + clause + preposition; the relative word can be left out

pitfalls.zh: 介词后面不能接 that 指人：不说 the man about that I spoke。
pitfalls.en: Never put that right after a preposition: the man about that I spoke is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 正式文书里介词常提前，留在句尾是口语做法。
pitfalls.en: Formal writing prefers the preposition first; the stranded form belongs to speech.

examples.text: This is the song I told you about.
examples.zh: 这就是我跟你说过的那首歌。

examples.text: The chair you are sitting on is very old.
examples.zh: 你坐的那把椅子很旧了。

explain.zh: 说完一句肯定的话，想请对方点头，就在后面挂一个否定的小问句：You're coming, aren't you? 前句肯定，附加部分就用否定，助动词照抄前句。语气比直接发问柔和，像把话递回去让对方接。
explain.en: After a positive statement, add a short negative question to invite agreement: You're coming, aren't you? The statement is positive, the tag is negative, and the tag repeats the auxiliary of the statement. It sounds softer than a plain question because it hands the conversation back to the other person.

form.zh: 肯定陈述 + 否定 tag；助动词与前句一致
form.en: positive statement + negative tag; the tag repeats the auxiliary

pitfalls.zh: I am 的 tag 是 aren't I，不是 am not I。
pitfalls.en: The tag for I am is aren't I, never am not I.

pitfalls.zh: tag 里的助动词必须跟前句一致，不能一律用 do。
pitfalls.en: The tag must reuse the auxiliary of the statement, not a default do.

examples.text: You're coming to the party, aren't you?
examples.zh: 你会来参加聚会，对吧？

examples.text: It's cold today, isn't it?
examples.zh: 今天挺冷的，是吧？

explain.zh: 前句带否定，附加的小问句就反过来用肯定：She isn't here, is she? 句中有 not、never、hardly 都算否定，tag 取肯定形式。用它确认自己没听错，或等对方点头。
explain.en: When the statement is negative, the tag turns positive: She isn't here, is she? A sentence containing not, never or hardly counts as negative, so the tag takes the positive form. You use it to check that you have heard right, or to wait for the other person to agree.

form.zh: 否定陈述 + 肯定 tag；助动词与前句一致
form.en: negative statement + positive tag; the tag repeats the auxiliary

pitfalls.zh: 前句已有 not，tag 不再加 not，否则双重否定。
pitfalls.en: The statement already has not, so the tag takes no not; otherwise you double the negative.

pitfalls.zh: never、hardly 也算否定，tag 照样用肯定。
pitfalls.en: Never and hardly make the statement negative too, so the tag stays positive.

examples.text: She doesn't eat meat, does she?
examples.zh: 她不吃肉，对吧？

examples.text: You didn't tell him, did you?
examples.zh: 你没告诉他吧？

name.zh: 功能疑问句：Couldn't you…?（委婉请求）

explain.zh: 请人帮忙时用否定问法 Couldn't you…?，比 Can you…? 客气，还带点「你能不能就…」的商量口气：Couldn't you stay a little longer? 后面接动词原形，多用在熟人之间，或对方已经知道你要什么的时候。
explain.en: When you ask a favour, the negative question Couldn't you…? sounds more tactful than Can you…?, with a hint of 'could you just…': Couldn't you stay a little longer? A base verb follows. It suits people you know, especially when they already know what you are after.

form.zh: Couldn't you + 动词原形？
form.en: Couldn't you + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: 后面接动词原形，不说 Couldn't you to help。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb after it: Couldn't you to help is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 否定问法带催促味道，对上级或陌生人少用。
pitfalls.en: The negative form can sound pushing, so avoid it with strangers or superiors.

examples.text: Couldn't you stay a little longer?
examples.zh: 你就不能多待一会儿吗？

examples.text: Couldn't you ask him for me?
examples.zh: 你不能替我问他一下吗？

name.zh: 功能疑问句：Wouldn't you…?（委婉请求）

explain.zh: Wouldn't you…? 把请求藏进建议里：Wouldn't you like to sit down? 听着像替对方打算。最常见的搭配是 Wouldn't you like + 名词或 to do，问对方想不想要；也可接动词原形请人做事，比 Will you…? 更婉转。
explain.en: Wouldn't you…? wraps a request inside a suggestion: Wouldn't you like to sit down? It sounds as if you are thinking of the other person. The usual pattern is Wouldn't you like + noun or to do, asking what someone would enjoy; a base verb also works for a very gentle request, softer than Will you…?

form.zh: Wouldn't you (like to) + 动词原形？
form.en: Wouldn't you (like to) + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: Wouldn't you like 后接名词或 to do，不直接接原形。
pitfalls.en: After Wouldn't you like, use a noun or to do, not a bare verb.

pitfalls.zh: 劝人时用降调，升调会显得在质疑对方。
pitfalls.en: Use a falling tone when you offer; a rise sounds like you doubt the other person.

examples.text: Wouldn't you like to join us?
examples.zh: 你不想一起来吗？

examples.text: Wouldn't you like some water?
examples.zh: 你要不要喝点水？

explain.zh: 想请人允许自己做一件事，用 May I 起头最客气：May I come in? 后面接动词原形。进办公室、借东西、问长辈都用它；朋友之间倒常换回 Can I，说法一样但没那么拘谨。
explain.en: To ask permission to do something yourself, May I is the most polite opening: May I come in? A base verb follows. Use it to enter an office, borrow something or speak to someone older; between friends Can I is the usual swap, same meaning with less formality.

form.zh: May I + 动词原形？答 Yes, you may. 或 No, you may not.
form.en: May I + base verb? Answer Yes, you may. or No, you may not.

pitfalls.zh: May I 后接动词原形，不说 May I to come in。
pitfalls.en: A base verb follows May I: May I to come in is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 回答用 you，不说 Yes, I may。
pitfalls.en: Answer with you, not Yes, I may.

examples.text: May I use your phone?
examples.zh: 我可以用一下你的电话吗？

examples.text: May I open the window?
examples.zh: 我可以开窗吗？

explain.zh: 想说「不如…」，就在形容词或副词前加 less，比较对象用 than 引出：less careful than…。它是 more 的反方向，长一点的形容词用它最省事。最高级再加上 the，成为 the least：the least expensive。
explain.en: To say something ranks lower, put less before the adjective or adverb and bring in the second item with than: less careful than…. It is the mirror image of more and works best with longer adjectives. For the superlative, add the and you get the least: the least expensive.

form.zh: less + 形容词/副词 (+ than…)；最高级 the least + 形容词
form.en: less + adjective/adverb (+ than …); superlative the least + adjective

pitfalls.zh: 别把 less 和 -er 叠着用：不说 less cheaper。
pitfalls.en: Do not stack less with -er: less cheaper is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 不可数用 less，可数名词的「更少」用 fewer。
pitfalls.en: Less goes with uncountable nouns; countable ones take fewer.

examples.text: This bag is less heavy than mine.
examples.zh: 这个包比我的轻。

examples.text: He drives less carefully than his brother.
examples.zh: 他开车不如他哥哥小心。

explain.zh: 说将来某件事「会被…」，用 will be + 过去分词：The results will be announced tomorrow。谁做的不重要或不知道时就用它，重点落在事情和结果上。否定把 not 放在 will 后面。
explain.en: For something that will be done later, use will be + past participle: The results will be announced tomorrow. Use it when the doer is unknown or unimportant, so the focus stays on the event and its result. The negative puts not after will.

form.zh: will be + 过去分词；否定 will not be + 过去分词
form.en: will be + past participle; negative will not be + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 别漏掉 be：不说 will announced。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop be: will announced is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 没有宾语的动词不能变被动，happen 就没有被动。
pitfalls.en: Verbs with no object have no passive, so happen cannot be passive.

examples.text: The new school will be opened next month.
examples.zh: 新学校下个月启用。

examples.text: Your order will be sent on Friday.
examples.zh: 你的订单周五寄出。

explain.zh: 动词后面接 to do 时，要否定后面那个动作，就把 not 塞在 to 前面：decide not to go。not 属于后面的不定式，不属于前面的动词，所以 don't decide to go 否定的是「决定」这件事，意思完全不同。
explain.en: When a verb is followed by to do and you need to negate that action, slip not in before to: decide not to go. The not belongs to the infinitive, not to the first verb, which is why don't decide to go negates the decision itself and means something else entirely.

form.zh: 动词 + not + to do
form.en: verb + not + to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: not 要放在 to 前面，不说 decide to not go。
pitfalls.en: Put not before to: decide to not go is not the standard form.

pitfalls.zh: 别把 not 提到主动词，don't decide to go 是另一个意思。
pitfalls.en: Do not move not onto the first verb; don't decide to go means something different.

examples.text: She decided not to buy the car.
examples.zh: 她决定不买那辆车了。

examples.text: He promised not to tell anyone.
examples.zh: 他答应不告诉任何人。

name.zh: 同位语从句 the fact that

explain.zh: 要把一整句话当名词塞进句里，先摆 the fact，再用 that 引出内容：the fact that he lied。这个短语能作主语，也能作宾语，that 后面必须是完整的主谓结构，不能只跟一个词。
explain.en: To use a whole statement as a noun inside a sentence, put the fact first and let that introduce the content: the fact that he lied. The phrase can be the subject or the object of a sentence, and a full clause with its own subject and verb must follow that.

form.zh: the fact that + 完整从句；可作主语或宾语
form.en: the fact that + full clause; the phrase works as subject or object

pitfalls.zh: that 后要完整句子，不能只接名词或短语。
pitfalls.en: A full clause follows that, never a bare noun or phrase.

pitfalls.zh: the 不能省：不说 I know fact that he left。
pitfalls.en: Keep the article: I know fact that he left is wrong.

examples.text: The fact that she apologized surprised us.
examples.zh: 她道了歉，这让我们很意外。

examples.text: We accept the fact that the plan may fail.
examples.zh: 我们接受计划可能失败这一事实。

name.zh: 形式宾语 it + 形容词 + to do

explain.zh: 想说觉得做某事怎么样，让 it 先占住宾语的位置，把真正的动作挪到句尾：I find it hard to say。形容词说明「做这件事」的性质，for + 人 点出对谁而言。句子不必靠一个长不定式打头，读起来更稳。
explain.en: To say how you find doing something, let it hold the object slot and move the real action to the end: I find it hard to say. The adjective describes the action, and for + person says who it applies to. The sentence no longer has to start with a long infinitive, so it is easier to follow.

form.zh: 动词 + it + 形容词 + (for + 人) + to do
form.en: verb + it + adjective + (for + person) + to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: it 不能换成 this 或 that，它只是占位的空宾语。
pitfalls.en: The it cannot become this or that; it is only a placeholder.

pitfalls.zh: 真正的动作在句尾，别说 I find hard to say。
pitfalls.en: The real action goes at the end; I find hard to say is wrong.

examples.text: I find it hard to get up early.
examples.zh: 我觉得早起很难。

examples.text: We consider it rude to interrupt.
examples.zh: 我们认为打断别人不礼貌。

explain.zh: whatever、whoever、wherever、however 的意思是「不管哪一个、谁、哪里、多么」，把两个分句压成一句：whatever you want。这些词自带「无论」，前面不用再加 no matter，后接自己的从句就行。
explain.en: Whatever, whoever, wherever and however mean 'no matter which, who, where or how', squeezing two clauses into one: whatever you want. Each -ever word already carries the 'no matter' idea, so no matter is never added in front; the word simply takes its own clause.

form.zh: whatever / whoever / wherever / however + 从句
form.en: whatever / whoever / wherever / however + clause

pitfalls.zh: 前面不再加 no matter，意思重复。
pitfalls.en: Do not add no matter in front; the meaning is already there.

pitfalls.zh: however 后接形容词或副词，不接完整句子。
pitfalls.en: However takes an adjective or adverb, not a whole clause.

examples.text: Take whatever you need from the box.
examples.zh: 箱子里需要什么就拿什么。

examples.text: Wherever you go, send me a message.
examples.zh: 不管你去哪儿，都给我发个消息。

explain.zh: 对眼下的状况不满意、但愿不是这样，用 wish + 过去式：I wish I knew。这里的过去式不指过去，只表示「跟现在的事实相反」。be 动词一律用 were，I wish I were taller。
explain.en: When you are unhappy with how things are and wish they were different, use wish + a past form: I wish I knew. The past form does not point to past time; it marks the wish as contrary to the present. With be, use were for every person: I wish I were taller.

form.zh: wish + 过去式；be 动词用 were
form.en: wish + past simple; were for all persons with be

pitfalls.zh: wish 后不用现在式：不说 I wish I know。
pitfalls.en: No present tense after wish: I wish I know is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 与现在相反时说 were，不说 I wish I would be。
pitfalls.en: For the present, say were: not I wish I would be.

examples.text: I wish I had more time.
examples.zh: 真希望我时间多一点。

examples.text: She wishes she lived by the sea.
examples.zh: 她希望自己住在海边。

explain.zh: 一件事从过去开始、现在还在继续，而你想强调「一直在做」，就用 have/has been + -ing：I've been waiting for an hour。常跟 for、since 连用；也能说刚停下的动作，结果还看得见。
explain.en: When something began in the past, is still going on, and you want to stress that it has been continuous, use have/has been + -ing: I've been waiting for an hour. It often comes with for or since, and it can also describe an action that has just stopped while its results are still there.

form.zh: have/has been + 动词 -ing；否定 haven't been + -ing
form.en: have/has been + -ing form; negative haven't/hasn't been + -ing

pitfalls.zh: 别漏掉 been：不说 I have waiting。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop been: I have waiting is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 说做了几次或已经做完，用现在完成时，不用进行。
pitfalls.en: For a count or a finished result, use the simple perfect, not the progressive.

examples.text: It has been raining since morning.
examples.zh: 从早上起一直在下雨。

examples.text: They have been looking for the key all day.
examples.zh: 他们找了一整天钥匙。

explain.zh: 要交代做一件事的目的，用 in order to + 动词原形：I left early in order to catch the train。它比光用 to 清楚，句子结构容易看混时尤其好用；否定写成 in order not to。
explain.en: To state the purpose of an action, use in order to + base verb: I left early in order to catch the train. It is clearer than a bare to, especially when the sentence is easy to misread, and the negative is in order not to.

form.zh: in order to + 动词原形；否定 in order not to + 动词原形
form.en: in order to + base verb; negative in order not to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: to 后接动词原形，不说 in order to catching。
pitfalls.en: A base verb follows to: in order to catching is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 目的的主语要和主句主语一致，否则指错人。
pitfalls.en: The doer of the purpose must be the subject of the main clause.

examples.text: She spoke slowly in order to be understood.
examples.zh: 她放慢语速，好让人听懂。

examples.text: We left early in order not to miss the bus.
examples.zh: 我们早早出发，免得错过公交车。

name.zh: 分词构句（-ing 置于句首）

explain.zh: 同一个人做两个动作，可以把其中一个改成 -ing 放到句首，句子就紧凑了：Walking home, I met her。句首这部分交代时间、原因或伴随的情况，主句的主语必须就是做这个动作的人。
explain.en: When one person does two things, turn one of them into an -ing phrase at the front and the sentence tightens up: Walking home, I met her. The opening phrase gives the time, the reason or the accompanying action, and the subject of the main clause must be the person doing it.

form.zh: 动词 -ing + 逗号 + 主句
form.en: -ing phrase + comma + main clause

pitfalls.zh: 分词的主语必须与主句一致，否则成了悬垂分词。
pitfalls.en: The participle needs the same subject as the main clause, or it dangles.

pitfalls.zh: 句首不加 when 或 and，直接把 -ing 部分放上去。
pitfalls.en: Do not add when or and; the -ing phrase stands on its own.

examples.text: Opening the door, she saw a letter on the floor.
examples.zh: 她打开门，看见地上有一封信。

examples.text: Not knowing the way, we asked a policeman.
examples.zh: 我们不认识路，就问了警察。

name.zh: 虚拟条件句（与现在相反）

explain.zh: 假设跟现在的事实相反，或眼下不太可能发生，if 从句用过去式，主句用 would + 动词原形：If I were you, I'd say no。过去式只表示「不是真的」，结果由 would 承担。
explain.en: For a condition that is contrary to present fact, or unlikely right now, the if-clause takes a past form and the main clause takes would + base verb: If I were you, I'd say no. The past form only marks the condition as unreal, while would carries the imagined result.

form.zh: If + 过去式，主句 would + 动词原形；be 用 were
form.en: If + past simple, would + base verb; were for all persons

pitfalls.zh: 主句用 would，不用 will：不说 If I had time, I will go。
pitfalls.en: The main clause takes would, not will: If I had time, I will go is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: if 从句里不用 would：不说 If I would be you。
pitfalls.en: No would inside the if-clause: If I would be you is wrong.

examples.text: If I had a car, I would drive you home.
examples.zh: 我要是有车，就开车送你回家。

examples.text: If she knew the answer, she would tell us.
examples.zh: 她要是知道答案，就会告诉我们。

name.zh: 倒装 so + 助动词 + 主语

explain.zh: 别人说了件肯定的事，你想说「我也一样」，就用 So + 助动词 + 主语：So do I。助动词要跟前一句对上，前句用 be、have 还是情态动词，就跟着用哪个。主语放在助动词后面，不能照正常语序。
explain.en: When someone makes a positive statement and you want to say the same is true of you, use So + auxiliary + subject: So do I. The auxiliary must match the first sentence, whether that was be, have or a modal. The subject follows the auxiliary instead of coming first.

form.zh: so + 助动词 + 主语
form.en: so + auxiliary + subject

pitfalls.zh: 助动词要跟前句一致，前句用 can 就说 So can I。
pitfalls.en: Match the auxiliary: if the first sentence has can, say So can I.

pitfalls.zh: 表示「我也一样」时不能照正常语序说 So I do。
pitfalls.en: Do not keep normal word order: So I do does not mean 'me too'.

examples.text: She can swim, and so can her sister.
examples.zh: 她会游泳，她妹妹也会。

examples.text: He was tired, and so was I.
examples.zh: 他累了，我也累了。

name.zh: 倒装 neither/nor + 助动词 + 主语

explain.zh: 别人说了件否定的事，你想说「我也不」，就用 Neither 或 Nor + 助动词 + 主语：Neither do I。助动词照样跟前句来，主语放在它后面。neither 和 nor 在这里换着用，语气没差别。
explain.en: When someone makes a negative statement and you want to say the same is true of you, use Neither or Nor + auxiliary + subject: Neither do I. The auxiliary matches the first sentence again, with the subject after it. Neither and nor are interchangeable here and sound the same.

form.zh: Neither/Nor + 助动词 + 主语
form.en: Neither/Nor + auxiliary + subject

pitfalls.zh: neither 本身已是否定，后面不再加 not。
pitfalls.en: Neither is already negative, so no not is added.

pitfalls.zh: 助动词要跟前句一致，前句用 be 就说 Neither am I。
pitfalls.en: Match the auxiliary: with be in the first sentence, say Neither am I.

examples.text: She can't drive, and neither can he.
examples.zh: 她不会开车，他也不会。

examples.text: He hasn't read it, and nor have I.
examples.zh: 他没读过，我也没读过。

explain.zh: 把 Never、Seldom、Hardly、Little、No sooner 这类否定词搬到句首，后面就得倒装，助动词提到主语前面：Never have I seen such a thing。这种说法语气重，多出现在书面语或刻意强调的时候。
explain.en: Move a negative word such as Never, Seldom, Hardly, Little or No sooner to the front and the clause inverts, with the auxiliary before the subject: Never have I seen such a thing. The pattern is emphatic and turns up mostly in writing or in deliberate emphasis.

form.zh: 否定词 + 助动词 + 主语 + 动词
form.en: negative adverb + auxiliary + subject + verb

pitfalls.zh: 否定词提前后必须倒装，不说 Never I have seen。
pitfalls.en: Once the negative word leads, invert: Never I have seen is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: No sooner 后面配 than，不配 when。
pitfalls.en: No sooner pairs with than, never with when.

examples.text: Never have I heard such a story.
examples.zh: 我从没听过这样的故事。

examples.text: Seldom does he leave the house after dark.
examples.zh: 他天黑后很少出门。

explain.zh: 几个人互相做同一件事，就把 one another 放到动词或介词后面，意思是「彼此」。主语得是两个以上的人或物，动作是双向的：你对我、我对你。它不能自己当主语。
explain.en: When a group of people do the same thing to each other, put one another after the verb or preposition and it means 'each other'. The subject must be two or more people or things, and the action goes both ways: you to me, me to you. It cannot stand as the subject itself.

form.zh: 动词/介词 + one another（作宾语）
form.en: verb / preposition + one another (as the object)

pitfalls.zh: 主语必须是两个以上：一个人不能 help one another。
pitfalls.en: The subject must be plural: one person cannot help one another.

pitfalls.zh: 它不能作主语：不说 One another helped us。
pitfalls.en: It cannot be the subject: One another helped us is wrong.

examples.text: The neighbours help one another when it snows.
examples.zh: 下雪时，邻居们互相帮忙。

examples.text: After the argument, they stopped talking to one another.
examples.zh: 那次争吵之后，他们就不跟对方说话了。

name.zh: the other / the others（另一个 / 其余）

explain.zh: 已经点出一个或一部分，剩下的那个用 the other，剩下的一群用 the others。两个词都指双方心里都清楚的那部分，后面不再接名词。
explain.en: When one item or one part of a group has already been named, use the other for the one that remains and the others for the ones that remain. Both point to a part that both speakers already have in mind, and no noun follows them.

form.zh: the other（单数）/ the others（复数）
form.en: the other (singular) / the others (plural)

pitfalls.zh: the others 已经代替复数名词，后面不再加名词。
pitfalls.en: the others already replaces a plural noun, so do not add one after it.

pitfalls.zh: 两个中剩下的一个用 the other，不用 the others。
pitfalls.en: For the one left out of two, use the other, not the others.

examples.text: One of my gloves is here; where is the other?
examples.zh: 我的一只手套在这儿，另一只呢？

examples.text: Three students passed and the others will try again.
examples.zh: 三个学生通过了，其余的要再试一次。

explain.zh: 要说「够……到能做某事」，把 enough 放在形容词或副词后面，后面常接 to do 点明够到哪一步。它只管程度够不够，不用来修饰名词。
explain.en: To say that something reaches the level needed, put enough after an adjective or adverb. A to-infinitive often follows to show what that level makes possible. It only talks about degree, not about quantity of a noun.

form.zh: 形容词/副词 + enough（+ to do）
form.en: adjective / adverb + enough (+ to + verb)

pitfalls.zh: enough 要放在形容词后面：不说 enough old。
pitfalls.en: Put enough after the adjective: enough old is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 副词也一样后置：fast enough，不是 enough fast。
pitfalls.en: Adverbs follow the same order: fast enough, not enough fast.

examples.text: The water is warm enough for a swim.
examples.zh: 水够暖，可以游泳了。

examples.text: She ran fast enough to catch the bus.
examples.zh: 她跑得够快，赶上了公交车。

explain.zh: 想说「这么……的一个东西」，就把 such 放在 a/an 前面，再接形容词和名词。它把程度说得很重，常带惊讶的口气，也常用来说明结果。
explain.en: To call something an extreme example of its kind, put such before a/an, then the adjective and the noun. It makes the degree feel heavy, often with surprise, and it is a common way to set up a result.

form.zh: such + a/an + 形容词 + 名词
form.en: such + a/an + adjective + noun

pitfalls.zh: a/an 要跟在 such 后面：不说 a such nice day。
pitfalls.en: Keep a/an after such: a such nice day is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 复数或不可数名词前不用 a/an：such nice weather。
pitfalls.en: No a/an before a plural or uncountable noun: such nice weather.

examples.text: It was such a cold morning that we stayed inside.
examples.zh: 那天早上太冷了，我们就留在屋里。

examples.text: I have never seen such a beautiful garden.
examples.zh: 我从没见过这么漂亮的花园。

explain.zh: 要给一句硬一点的劝告或提醒，就用 had better 加动词原形，意思是「最好……」。它暗示不这么做会出麻烦，语气比 should 强，后面不带 to。
explain.en: To give firm advice or a warning, use had better with the base form of the verb, meaning that something bad may follow if it is ignored. It is stronger than should and takes no to.

form.zh: had better + 动词原形；否定 had better not + 动词原形
form.en: had better + base verb; negative had better not + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 后面直接接动词原形，不加 to。
pitfalls.en: The base verb follows directly, with no to.

pitfalls.zh: had 在这里不表示过去，别改成 have better。
pitfalls.en: had here is not about past time, so do not change it to have better.

examples.text: You had better take an umbrella; it looks like rain.
examples.zh: 你最好带把伞，看样子要下雨。

examples.text: We had better not be late again.
examples.zh: 我们最好别再迟到了。

explain.zh: 事情已经这样、也没有更好的办法，就说 might as well 加动词原形，意思是「不妨……、还不如……」。它表示这么做没什么损失，语气随意。
explain.en: When things are already the way they are and no better option is left, say might as well with the base verb, meaning there is no harm in doing it. It suggests nothing is lost by trying, and the tone is casual.

form.zh: might as well + 动词原形
form.en: might as well + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 这里的 might 不表推测，别译成「也许会」。
pitfalls.en: might here is not about possibility, so do not read it as 'perhaps'.

pitfalls.zh: 后面直接接动词原形，不加 to。
pitfalls.en: The base verb follows directly, with no to.

examples.text: The train is late, so we might as well have a coffee.
examples.zh: 火车晚点了，我们不妨喝杯咖啡。

examples.text: There is nothing to do here, so we might as well go home.
examples.zh: 这儿没什么可做的，我们不如回家。

explain.zh: 在两个选择里说自己更想要哪个，就用 would rather 加动词原形，意思是「宁愿……」。它只讲说话人自己的偏好，比 prefer 直接，比较另一个选择时用 than。
explain.en: To say which of two choices you prefer, use would rather with the base verb, meaning you would like one more than the other. It states the speaker's own preference, more directly than prefer, and than introduces the other choice.

form.zh: would rather + 动词原形；对比用 than + 动词原形
form.en: would rather + base verb; than + base verb for the other choice

pitfalls.zh: 后面直接接动词原形，不加 to。
pitfalls.en: The base verb follows directly, with no to.

pitfalls.zh: would 不能省：只说 rather stay 句子不完整。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop would: rather stay on its own is not a full sentence.

examples.text: I would rather walk than take the bus.
examples.zh: 我宁愿走路，也不坐公交。

examples.text: Would you rather stay in tonight?
examples.zh: 你今晚宁愿待在家里吗？

explain.zh: 句子里要夹一句「是不是」，就把 whether 放在 know、ask、wonder 这类动词后面，让它带出这个小句子。它引出两种可能，表示拿不准或需要确认。
explain.en: When a yes-or-no question sits inside a sentence, put whether after verbs like know, ask or wonder and let it bring in that short clause. It presents two possibilities and signals uncertainty or a need to check.

form.zh: whether + 陈述语序；可接 or not
form.en: whether + subject + verb in statement order; or not may follow

pitfalls.zh: 从句用陈述语序：whether it was，不是 whether was it。
pitfalls.en: Keep statement order in the clause: whether it was, not whether was it.

pitfalls.zh: 介词后、句首、与 or not 连用时用 whether，不用 if。
pitfalls.en: Use whether after a preposition, at the start of a sentence, and with or not; if does not work there.

examples.text: I don't know whether the shop is open today.
examples.zh: 我不知道那家店今天开不开门。

examples.text: She asked whether we had finished the report.
examples.zh: 她问我们报告写完了没有。

name.zh: 时间状语从句 by the time

explain.zh: 要说「到某个时候为止，另一件事已经怎样了」，先摆 by the time 加一句，再讲主句。它把两件事排成先后，主句常用完成时，或加上 already。
explain.en: To say how far one event had gone by a certain moment, start with by the time and a clause, then give the main clause. It lines the two events up in order, and the main clause often takes a perfect tense or already.

form.zh: by the time + 从句，主句常用完成时
form.en: by the time + clause; the main clause often takes a perfect tense

pitfalls.zh: 后面要接完整句子，不能只接名词：不说 by the time Monday。
pitfalls.en: A full clause must follow: by the time Monday is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 讲过去的事，主句用过去完成时：had left。
pitfalls.en: For past time, the main clause usually takes the past perfect: had left.

examples.text: By the time we reached the cinema, the film had started.
examples.zh: 我们到电影院时，电影已经开场了。

examples.text: By the time you read this, I will have left.
examples.zh: 你读到这些的时候，我已经走了。

name.zh: 形式宾语 it + 形容词 + that 从句

explain.zh: 觉得某件事奇怪、重要或清楚，就先把 it 放在动词后面占个位，形容词紧跟其后，真正的内容用 that 从句搁到句尾。it 本身没有意思，只是替从句腾位置。
explain.en: When you want to judge a fact as strange, important or clear, put it after the verb as a placeholder, let the adjective follow, and move the real content into a that-clause at the end. The it means nothing on its own; it simply holds the place.

form.zh: 动词 + it + 形容词 + that 从句
form.en: verb + it + adjective + that-clause

pitfalls.zh: it 不能省：不说 I find strange that he left。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop it: I find strange that he left is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 从句用 that 引导，别换成 if 或 because。
pitfalls.en: The clause takes that, not if or because.

examples.text: I find it strange that nobody called us.
examples.zh: 我觉得奇怪，没人给我们打电话。

examples.text: She made it clear that the meeting was cancelled.
examples.zh: 她说清楚了会议取消了。

explain.zh: 要说明某样东西属于谁，就用 whose 引出后面那句，whose 后面直接接那个东西。它顶掉 his、her、their 这类词，把两句话并成一句，人和物都能用。
explain.en: To say who something belongs to, use whose to open the describing clause and put the owned thing straight after it. It replaces his, her or their and joins two sentences into one, and it works for people and things alike.

form.zh: 名词 + whose + 名词 + 动词
form.en: noun + whose + noun + verb

pitfalls.zh: whose 后直接接东西，别再补 his/her：whose his car。
pitfalls.en: The owned thing follows whose directly, with no his or her: whose his car is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 别跟 who's 混：whose 表所属，who's 是 who is。
pitfalls.en: Do not mix it up with who's: whose shows possession, who's means who is.

examples.text: The woman whose son plays in our team lives next door.
examples.zh: 儿子在我们队里踢球的那位女士就住在隔壁。

examples.text: I met a writer whose books I have read.
examples.zh: 我遇到了一位作家，他的书我读过。

name.zh: get + 宾语 + 现在分词

explain.zh: 要让某人或某物动起来，就用 get 加上那个东西，再接动词的 -ing 形式。重点在「让它开始动、跑起来」，动作还在继续。
explain.en: To make someone or something start moving or working, use get, then that person or thing, then the -ing form of the verb. The focus is on setting it going, with the action still under way.

form.zh: get + 宾语 + 动词-ing
form.en: get + object + verb-ing

pitfalls.zh: 用 -ing 形式，别换成原形：不说 get the car run。
pitfalls.en: Use the -ing form, not the base verb: get the car run is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 宾语要放在 -ing 前面：不说 get running the car。
pitfalls.en: The object comes before the -ing form: get running the car is wrong.

examples.text: He got the old engine running again.
examples.zh: 他把那台旧发动机又发动起来了。

examples.text: The music soon got everyone dancing.
examples.zh: 音乐很快就让大家跳起舞来。

name.zh: as if / as though + 过去式

explain.zh: 把眼前的事说成「好像……」，可心里并不当真，就在 as if 后面用过去式。整句讲的是现在，动词却退一步用过去，表示和事实相反。
explain.en: To describe the present as if something were true, when you do not believe it is, use the past tense after as if. The sentence is about now, but the verb steps back into the past to show it is contrary to fact.

form.zh: as if / as though + 过去式
form.en: as if / as though + past simple

pitfalls.zh: 讲现在的事别用现在时：不说 as if he knows。
pitfalls.en: For present meaning, do not use the present tense: as if he knows is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 很可能为真就用陈述语气：looks as if it is raining。
pitfalls.en: When it is probably true, use the ordinary tense: it looks as if it is raining.

examples.text: He talks as if he owned the whole company.
examples.zh: 他说话的口气好像整个公司都是他的。

examples.text: He behaved as though nothing mattered to him.
examples.zh: 他那副样子，好像什么都不在乎。

explain.zh: 想强调「确实、真的」，就在动词前加 do 或 does，后面的动词回到原形。别人怀疑你、或你要把话顶回去时用它；肯定句本来不需要助动词，加了它语气就重了。
explain.en: To stress that something really is true, put do or does before the verb and leave the verb in its base form. Use it when someone doubts you or when you want to push back; positive sentences need no auxiliary, so adding one makes the statement stronger.

form.zh: do/does + 动词原形（第三人称单数用 does）
form.en: do/does + base verb; does with a third-person singular subject

pitfalls.zh: 只在强调时加，普通陈述句别加 do。
pitfalls.en: Add it only for emphasis; a plain statement takes no do.

pitfalls.zh: 用了 does，后面动词必须还原：不说 does likes。
pitfalls.en: After does the verb goes back to base form: not does likes.

examples.text: I do like your new jacket.
examples.zh: 我确实喜欢你新买的夹克。

examples.text: She does want to come with us.
examples.zh: 她真的很想跟我们一起来。

explain.zh: 讲过去的事，要在肯定句上加重语气，就用 did + 动词原形。反驳别人、或强调自己真的做过某件事时用它；did 已经带了过去时，后面不再变形。
explain.en: To add force to a positive sentence about the past, use did plus the base verb. It fits when you are contradicting someone or insisting that something really happened; did already carries the past tense, so the verb after it stays unchanged.

form.zh: did + 动词原形（否定用 did not + 原形）
form.en: did + base verb; did not + base verb in the negative

pitfalls.zh: 普通过去叙述用一般过去时，不加 did。
pitfalls.en: For ordinary past narration, use the simple past without did.

pitfalls.zh: did 后面动词回原形：不说 did saw。
pitfalls.en: The verb after did is a base form: not did saw.

examples.text: I did call you twice yesterday.
examples.zh: 我昨天确实给你打了两次电话。

examples.text: He did finish the report on time.
examples.zh: 他确实按时完成了报告。

explain.zh: 讲过去的事，要补一句「在那之前就已经……」，用 had + 过去分词。它把时间再往前推一步：交代背景、补更早的原因，或分清两件过去的事谁先谁后，常和一般过去时同现。
explain.en: When you are already talking about the past and need to say that something had happened even earlier, use had plus the past participle. It steps one stage further back to give background, an earlier cause, or the order of two past events, and it usually appears alongside the simple past.

form.zh: had + 过去分词；否定 had not done，问句 Had you done…?
form.en: had + past participle; had not + past participle; Had you + past participle…?

pitfalls.zh: 句里要先有另一件更晚的过去事情；只有一件过去事就用一般过去时。
pitfalls.en: A later past event has to come first in the sentence; for a single past event, use the simple past.

pitfalls.zh: had gone、had been 只把时间往前推，不等于「刚刚」或「很久以前」。
pitfalls.en: Had gone and had been only move the action earlier; they do not mean just now or long ago.

examples.text: When we got to the cinema, the film had already begun.
examples.zh: 我们到电影院时，电影已经开演了。

examples.text: By the time the boat reached shore, the sun had set.
examples.zh: 船靠岸时，太阳已经落下。

explain.zh: 说某件事「可以／必须／应该被……」，就用情态动词 + be + 过去分词。谁做的不重要或说不清时用它，重点落在事情本身；情态动词后面固定用 be，不再管单复数。
