explain.en: To say that something can, must or should be done, use a modal verb plus be and the past participle. It fits when who does it is unknown or unimportant, so the focus stays on the action itself; be never changes form after a modal.

form.zh: 情态动词 + be + 过去分词（否定 + not be）
form.en: modal + be + past participle; modal + not be + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 情态动词后一定用 be：不说 can is done。
pitfalls.en: Be always follows the modal: not can is done.

pitfalls.zh: be 后面接过去分词，不接原形或 -ing。
pitfalls.en: Be takes a past participle here, not a base form or an -ing form.

examples.text: This form must be signed by Friday.
examples.zh: 这张表必须在周五前签字。

examples.text: The room can be booked online.
examples.zh: 这个房间可以在网上预订。

name.zh: 否定不定式 not to do

explain.zh: 要说「不去做、别做」某件事，就把 not 放在 to 前面，写成 not to do。它常跟着 decide、ask、tell 这类动词走，也可以放在句首表示目的的反面。
explain.en: To express not doing something, put not before to and write not to do. It commonly follows verbs like decide, ask and tell, and it can also open a sentence to say what someone avoided doing.

form.zh: not + to + 动词原形
form.en: not + to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 别写成 to not do，教科书顺序是 not to do。
pitfalls.en: Do not write to not do; the textbook order is not to do.

pitfalls.zh: not 不能换成 don't：不说 don't to go。
pitfalls.en: Not cannot be replaced by don't: not don't to go.

examples.text: She decided not to take the job.
examples.zh: 她决定不接受这份工作。

examples.text: I asked him not to be late again.
examples.zh: 我让他别再迟到。

name.zh: be to do（按计划 / 应当）

explain.zh: 说「按安排将要……」或「按规定应当……」，用 be to + 动词原形。它多出现在通知、日程、规定里，口气比 will 硬，带一点已经定好、不由个人改的意思。
explain.en: Use be plus to and a base verb for something due to happen by arrangement, or for what people are required to do. It belongs to notices, timetables and rules, and it sounds firmer than will, with a sense that the plan is already fixed.

form.zh: am/is/are to + 动词原形（否定 be not to）
form.en: am/is/are to + base verb; be not to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 日常随口说将来用 will 或 be going to，别处处用 be to。
pitfalls.en: For ordinary future talk use will or be going to, not be to everywhere.

pitfalls.zh: to 后面是动词原形，不加 -s 或 -ed。
pitfalls.en: A base verb follows to, with no -s or -ed.

examples.text: The train is to leave at six tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 这趟列车定于明天早上六点出发。

examples.text: You are not to touch these files.
examples.zh: 这些文件你不能碰。

explain.zh: 句子已经有主语，另一件事是被动发生的，就用 being + 过去分词放在句首。它相当于「因为被……／当被……时」，两个动作的主语是同一个，所以不用再写一遍。
explain.en: When a sentence already has a subject and a second action happens to that subject, open with being plus the past participle. It means because of being… or when being…, and since both actions share one subject, the subject is not repeated.

form.zh: Being + 过去分词，再接主句
form.en: Being + past participle, followed by the main clause

pitfalls.zh: 两个动作的主语必须一致，不一致就别这样省略。
pitfalls.en: Both actions need the same subject; if they differ, do not leave it out.

pitfalls.zh: 主语是动作的承受者，不是发出者。
pitfalls.en: The subject receives the action here; it does not perform it.

examples.text: Being asked about the delay, she said nothing.
examples.zh: 被问到延误的事，她什么也没说。

examples.text: Being watched by the crowd, the boy ran faster.
examples.zh: 被众人看着，那个男孩跑得更快了。

explain.zh: 回头猜或评一件已经发生的事，就用情态动词 + have + 过去分词。must have done 是「当时一定……了」，should have done 是「本该……却没做」，can't have done 是「不可能……」。
explain.en: To guess about or judge something that has already happened, use a modal verb plus have and the past participle. Must have done means it certainly happened, should have done means it was the right thing but did not happen, and can't have done means it is impossible.

form.zh: 情态动词 + have + 过去分词
form.en: modal + have + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 讲现在的情况直接加原形，别加 have done。
pitfalls.en: For a present situation use the base verb, not have done.

pitfalls.zh: have 后面是过去分词，不是原形：不说 must have go。
pitfalls.en: A past participle follows have: not must have go.

examples.text: They must have missed the last bus.
examples.zh: 他们一定是错过了末班车。

examples.text: You should have told me earlier.
examples.zh: 你本该早点告诉我。

name.zh: 感官动词 + 宾语 + 动词原形

explain.zh: 看见或听见某人把一件事做完了，用 see、hear 这类词 + 人 + 动词原形。你注意的是整件事发生了、从头到尾；中间不加 to，也不加 -ing。
explain.en: When you see or hear someone do something from start to finish, use see, hear and similar verbs plus a person and the base verb. The whole action happened, and no to or -ing comes in between.

form.zh: see/hear/feel + 宾语 + 动词原形
form.en: see/hear/feel + object + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 这里不加 to：不说 I saw him to leave。
pitfalls.en: No to goes here: not I saw him to leave.

pitfalls.zh: 只用于看见、听见一类词，think、know 不能这样用。
pitfalls.en: Only perception verbs like see and hear work this way, not think or know.

examples.text: I saw the man leave the building.
examples.zh: 我看见那个人离开了大楼。

examples.text: We heard her sing the whole song.
examples.zh: 我们听她唱完了整首歌。

name.zh: 感官动词 + 宾语 + 现在分词

explain.zh: 看见或听见某人正在做某事，用 see、hear 这类词 + 人 + 动词 -ing。你看到的是动作进行中的一段，还没结束，重点在那一刻的画面。
explain.en: When you see or hear someone in the middle of doing something, use see, hear and similar verbs plus a person and the -ing form. You catch one stretch of the action while it is still going on, and the focus is on that moment.

form.zh: see/hear/feel + 宾语 + 现在分词
form.en: see/hear/feel + object + present participle

pitfalls.zh: 动作正在进行才用 -ing，做完用动词原形。
pitfalls.en: Use -ing for an action in progress; for a finished action use the base verb.

pitfalls.zh: 宾语后直接接 -ing，不再加 to 或 be。
pitfalls.en: The -ing form follows the object directly, with no to or be.

examples.text: We heard the neighbors arguing again.
examples.zh: 我们又听见邻居在吵架。

examples.text: She saw a cat running across the road.
examples.zh: 她看见一只猫跑过马路。

explain.zh: 讲过去某件事之前一直在做的事，用 had been + 动词 -ing。它说明那个动作持续了一段时间，到那个过去时刻才停或还在继续，常和 when、before、for two hours 一起出现。
explain.en: Use had been plus the -ing form for something that had been going on before another past event. It shows the action lasted for a while up to that past moment, and it often appears with when, before or for two hours.

form.zh: had been + 现在分词
form.en: had been + present participle

pitfalls.zh: 只讲做过一次、没强调持续，用过去完成时。
pitfalls.en: For a single completed action with no sense of duration, use the past perfect.

pitfalls.zh: had been 后面一定是 -ing，不是过去分词。
pitfalls.en: An -ing form follows had been, not a past participle.

examples.text: She had been waiting for an hour when the bus came.
examples.zh: 公交车来时，她已经等了一个小时。

examples.text: They had been living in that flat for years.
examples.zh: 他们在那套公寓里已经住了好些年。

explain.zh: 说在将来某个时间点之前会把事做完，用 will have + 过去分词。常和 by then、by next June 这类终点一起出现；说话时还没做完，到那个时间就完成了。
explain.en: Use will have plus the past participle for something that will be finished before a point in the future. It usually comes with a deadline such as by then or by next June: the work is not done yet, but it will be by that time.

form.zh: will have + 过去分词（否定 will not have done）
form.en: will have + past participle; will not have + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 句里要有将来时间作终点，否则用一般将来时。
pitfalls.en: A future deadline is needed; otherwise use the simple future.

pitfalls.zh: will have 后面是过去分词，不是原形。
pitfalls.en: A past participle follows will have, not a base verb.

examples.text: By next June, we will have finished the whole course.
examples.zh: 到明年六月，我们就会学完整个课程。

examples.text: She will have left before you arrive.
examples.zh: 你到之前她就已经走了。

explain.zh: 说某件事此刻正在被做，用 am/is/are being + 过去分词。它表示动作正在进行，不是已经完成；主语是承受动作的一方，不是动手的人。
explain.en: Use am, is or are plus being and the past participle for something that is being done right now. The action is still in progress rather than finished, and the subject receives the action instead of performing it.

form.zh: am/is/are being + 过去分词
form.en: am/is/are being + past participle

pitfalls.zh: being 后面接过去分词：不说 is being repair。
pitfalls.en: A past participle follows being: not is being repair.

pitfalls.zh: 说平常的状态、不强调进行，用一般现在被动。
pitfalls.en: For a usual state rather than an action in progress, use the simple present passive.

examples.text: The bridge is being repaired this month.
examples.zh: 这座桥这个月正在维修。

examples.text: Your car is being washed right now.
examples.zh: 你的车正在洗。

name.zh: have/get + 宾语 + 过去分词

explain.zh: 事情不自己做、而是请人或让别人做，用 have/get + 东西 + 过去分词。也能说自己碰上不想要的事，比如钱包被偷；过去分词说明那件事对宾语做了什么。
explain.en: When someone else does the job for you instead of you doing it yourself, use have or get plus the thing and a past participle. It also covers unwanted experiences such as having your wallet stolen; the participle says what was done to the object.

form.zh: have/get + 宾语 + 过去分词
form.en: have/get + object + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 宾语是被怎么处理，不是它自己去做什么。
pitfalls.en: The object is acted on; it does not perform the action itself.

pitfalls.zh: 宾语后接过去分词，不接原形或 -ing。
pitfalls.en: A past participle follows the object, not a base form or -ing.

examples.text: We are having the kitchen painted next week.
examples.zh: 我们下周请人把厨房刷一遍。

examples.text: She got her phone stolen on the train.
examples.zh: 她的手机在火车上被偷了。

name.zh: 虚拟条件句（与过去相反）

explain.zh: 说过去本来会怎样、其实没发生，用 if + had + 过去分词，主句用 would have + 过去分词。两边讲的都是过去，事实正好相反；主句的 have 不能省。
explain.en: To say what would have happened in the past if things had been different, use if plus had and the past participle, then would have and the past participle in the main clause. Both halves look back on the past, and the facts were the opposite.

form.zh: If + had + 过去分词，主句 would have + 过去分词
form.en: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 主句用 would have done，不用 would do。
pitfalls.en: The main clause takes would have done, not would do.

pitfalls.zh: if 从句里不用 would：不说 If I would have known。
pitfalls.en: No would inside the if-clause: not If I would have known.

examples.text: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.
examples.zh: 要是我们早点走，就赶上那趟火车了。

examples.text: She would have passed the exam if she had studied.
examples.zh: 她要是复习了，本来能通过考试。

explain.zh: 表示建议、要求、命令的动词后面，that 从句里的动词用原形，不随主语加 -s，也不用 to。常见的有 suggest、insist、demand、require；英式英语里也常写成 should + 原形。
explain.en: After verbs of suggesting, demanding or ordering, the verb in the that-clause stays in the base form: no -s, no to. Common ones are suggest, insist, demand and require, and British English often uses should plus the base verb instead.

form.zh: suggest/insist + that + 主语 + 动词原形
form.en: suggest/insist + that + subject + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 从句动词不随主语变：不说 He suggested that she goes。
pitfalls.en: The clause verb does not agree with its subject: not He suggested that she goes.

pitfalls.zh: 这里不加 to，也不加 will。
pitfalls.en: No to and no will here.

examples.text: The doctor insisted that he stay in bed.
examples.zh: 医生坚持让他卧床休息。

examples.text: They demanded that the report be sent today.
examples.zh: 他们要求今天就把报告发出去。

name.zh: the + 比较级, the + 比较级

explain.zh: 两件事一起变，就用「the + 比较级 …, the + 比较级 …」：前半句是条件，后半句跟着它变。像「你练得越多，进步越大」，两个 the 都在句首，各自带自己的主语和动词，中间用逗号断开。
explain.en: To say that two things change together, use the + comparative in both halves: the first half names the condition, and the second half changes with it. Each the opens its own clause with its own subject and verb, and a comma separates the two halves.

form.zh: the + 比较级 + 主语 + 动词, the + 比较级 + 主语 + 动词
form.en: the + comparative + subject + verb, the + comparative + subject + verb

pitfalls.zh: 两个 the 都不能省：不说 More you practise, better you get。
pitfalls.en: Keep both the's: More you practise, better you get is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 前半句也别写成问句语序：不说 The more do you practise。
pitfalls.en: Do not use question order in the first half: The more do you practise is wrong.

examples.text: The more you practise, the more confident you become.
examples.zh: 你练得越多，就越自信。

examples.text: The older he gets, the quieter he becomes.
examples.zh: 他年纪越大，话越少。

name.zh: 动词 + 宾语 + not to do

explain.zh: 请别人「别做」某事，就把 not to 放在宾语后面：ask him not to go。not 否定的是后面那个动作，不是前面的动词，所以位置必须在宾语之后。常用在 ask、tell、want、advise、remind 这类动词后。
explain.en: When you want someone not to do something, put not to after the object: ask him not to go. The not denies the later action, not the first verb, so it must come after the object. Common verbs here are ask, tell, want, advise and remind.

form.zh: 动词 + 宾语 + not to + 动词原形
form.en: verb + object + not to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: not 别提前到动词前：不说 I asked not him to go。
pitfalls.en: Do not move not in front of the verb: I asked not him to go is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: not 后面别丢了 to：不说 She told me not go。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop to after not: She told me not go is wrong.

examples.text: She asked me not to tell anyone about the plan.
examples.zh: 她让我别把计划告诉任何人。

examples.text: The doctor advised him not to drive for a week.
examples.zh: 医生建议他一周内不要开车。

explain.zh: 要让一个 -ing 动作变成「没做」，把 not 直接放在 -ing 前面：not knowing what to say。这样写常放在句首或逗号后，说明当时没做某事，接着讲它带来什么结果。
explain.en: To make an -ing action negative, put not directly in front of it: not knowing what to say. This form often opens a sentence or follows a comma, saying what someone did not do and what came of it.

form.zh: not + 动词-ing；完成形式 not having + 过去分词
form.en: not + verb-ing; perfect form not having + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 否定词放 -ing 前面，不是后面：不说 knowing not the answer。
pitfalls.en: Put not before the -ing form, not after it: knowing not the answer is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 别写成 don't + -ing：不说 don't knowing what to do。
pitfalls.en: Do not use don't with -ing: don't knowing what to do is wrong.

examples.text: Not knowing anyone there, she sat alone by the window.
examples.zh: 她在那里谁也不认识，就独自坐在窗边。

examples.text: Not having a map, we stopped to ask a policeman.
examples.zh: 我们没有地图，就停下来问警察。

explain.zh: 两件事一先一后，把先做完的那件写成 Having + 过去分词，放在句首：Having finished, he left。它的意思接近「做完……之后」，主句讲随后发生的事，前后主语要是同一个人。
explain.en: When one action finishes before another, put the earlier one first as Having + past participle: Having finished, he left. It means much the same as after doing something, the main clause tells what happened next, and both parts share the same subject.

form.zh: Having + 过去分词, 主句；否定 Not having + 过去分词
form.en: Having + past participle, main clause; negative Not having + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 前后主语要一致：不说 Having finished, the door opened。
pitfalls.en: Keep one subject for both parts: Having finished, the door opened is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 先发生的放 Having 后，后发生的放主句，别颠倒。
pitfalls.en: Put the earlier action after Having and the later one in the main clause.

examples.text: Having read the letter twice, she put it down slowly.
examples.zh: 她把信读了两遍，才慢慢放下。

examples.text: Having lost his key, he waited outside the flat.
examples.zh: 他丢了钥匙，只好在公寓外面等。

explain.zh: 说「敢不敢」做某事，用 dare，后面接动词原形，带不带 to 都可以。否定和疑问里常把它当助动词用，直接写 dare not、Dare you …?，不再借 do；口语里也常说 didn't dare to。
explain.en: To talk about having the courage to do something, use dare with a base verb, with or without to. In negatives and questions it often works like a modal: dare not, Dare you …?, with no do added. In speech didn't dare to is also common.

form.zh: dare (to) + 动词原形；dare not + 动词原形；Dare you + 动词原形?
form.en: dare (to) + base verb; dare not + base verb; Dare you + base verb?

pitfalls.zh: dare 后别接 -ing 或过去式：不说 He dares going alone。
pitfalls.en: Do not put -ing or a past form after dare: He dares going alone is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 当助动词时别再加 does：不说 Does he dare not go?
pitfalls.en: As a modal it takes no does: Does he dare not go? is wrong.

examples.text: He didn't dare to look at her face.
examples.zh: 他不敢看她的脸。

examples.text: Dare you tell her the truth tonight?
examples.zh: 今晚你敢跟她说实话吗？

explain.zh: might 后面加 well，把握就更大：不只是「也许会」，而是「很可能，而且有理由这样」。常见的说法还有 might well be right、might well ask。well 在这里是固定搭配，不能省。
explain.en: Adding well to might makes the guess stronger: not just maybe, but quite likely and with good reason. Common patterns are might well be right and might well ask. The well is a fixed part of the phrase and cannot be left out.

form.zh: might well + 动词原形
form.en: might well + base verb

pitfalls.zh: well 别写成 good：不说 She might good be right。
pitfalls.en: Use well, not good: She might good be right is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: might 后不接 to：不说 He might well to win。
pitfalls.en: No to after might: He might well to win is wrong.

examples.text: She might well be right about the delay.
examples.zh: 关于延误这件事，她很可能说对了。

examples.text: You might well ask why nobody warned us.
examples.zh: 你完全有理由问，为什么没人提醒我们。

explain.zh: as 可以像关系代词一样，指代整个主句说的那件事，意思是「正如……」。固定说法有 as we know、as you can see、as was expected，通常用逗号隔开，放在句首或句中。
explain.en: As can stand in for a whole clause, much like a relative pronoun, and means just as or in the way that. Fixed patterns include as we know, as you can see and as was expected; they are set off by commas, at the start of a sentence or in the middle.

form.zh: as + 主语 + 动词，放句首或插在句中，前后用逗号隔开
form.en: as + subject + verb, at the start of a sentence or inside it, set off by commas

pitfalls.zh: 别用 like 顶替：不说 Like we know, the shop is shut。
pitfalls.en: Do not swap in like: Like we know, the shop is shut is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: as 后面要接完整小句，别只跟一个名词。
pitfalls.en: Let a full clause follow as, not a bare noun.

examples.text: As we know, the museum is closed on Mondays.
examples.zh: 正如我们所知，博物馆周一闭馆。

examples.text: The plan failed, as was expected.
examples.zh: 这个计划失败了，正如预料的那样。

name.zh: 强调句（强调介词短语、副词）
name.en: CLEFT SENTENCE FOCUSING ON PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE/ADVERB

explain.zh: 想突出时间、地点或方式，就把那部分状语塞进 It was … that 中间：It was in 1990 that …。去掉 It was 和 that，剩下的词照样能连成一句完整的话，这就是判断用得对不对的办法。
explain.en: To highlight a time, place or manner, move that adverbial into the frame It was … that: It was in 1990 that …. If you take away It was and that, the rest still makes a complete sentence, which is a good way to check the pattern.

form.zh: It is/was + 介词短语或副词 + that + 其余部分
form.en: It is/was + prepositional phrase or adverb + that + the rest

pitfalls.zh: that 后面不倒装：不说 It was in 1990 that did he arrive。
pitfalls.en: No inversion after that: It was in 1990 that did he arrive is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 被强调的状语要挪到 It was 后面，别留在句尾。
pitfalls.en: Move the focused adverbial after It was instead of leaving it at the end.

examples.text: It was in the garden that she found the ring.
examples.zh: 她是在花园里找到那枚戒指的。

examples.text: It was only last week that I heard the news.
examples.zh: 我上周才听到这个消息。

explain.zh: 想把重点提到句子前面，就用 What 开头：What I want is rest。What 带出的部分当主语，后面接 is 或 was，再接真正要强调的内容，语序和普通陈述句一样。
explain.en: To put the important part first, open with What: What I want is rest. The What clause works as the subject, then comes is or was, then the thing you really want to stress, all in ordinary statement order.

form.zh: What + 主语 + 动词 + is/was + 强调内容
form.en: What + subject + verb + is/was + the focused part

pitfalls.zh: What 从句用陈述语序：不说 What do I want is rest。
pitfalls.en: Keep statement order in the What clause: What do I want is rest is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: is 后面别再重复同一个动词：不说 What I want is want rest。
pitfalls.en: Do not repeat the verb after is: What I want is want rest is wrong.

examples.text: What I need is a quiet room.
examples.zh: 我需要的是一个安静的房间。

examples.text: What surprised me was his calm voice.
examples.zh: 让我吃惊的是他平静的声音。

name.zh: 感官动词 + 宾语 + 过去分词

explain.zh: 看见或听见某人某物「被……」时，在 see、hear、feel 的宾语后面接过去分词：I heard the song sung。宾语是承受动作的一方，所以用过去分词，不用 -ing。
explain.en: When you see or hear something being acted on, follow the object of see, hear or feel with a past participle: I heard the song sung. The object receives the action, which is why the past participle is used rather than the -ing form.

form.zh: see/hear/feel + 宾语 + 过去分词
form.en: see/hear/feel + object + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 别用 -ing 顶替：heard the song singing 意思就变成主动了。
pitfalls.en: Do not use -ing instead: heard the song singing makes the song the doer.

pitfalls.zh: 过去分词前别再补 be：不说 I saw the window be broken。
pitfalls.en: Do not add be before the participle: I saw the window be broken is wrong.

examples.text: I saw the window broken by the storm.
examples.zh: 我看见窗户被暴风雨打破了。

examples.text: We heard our names called at the gate.
examples.zh: 我们听见有人在门口叫我们的名字。

name.en: IF+SHOULD (e.g. if it should rain tomorrow)

explain.zh: 说「万一」发生某事，在 if 后面加 should：If it should rain, …。这比 if it rains 更没把握，也更客气，主句常接 will、can 或一句请求。
explain.en: To talk about something that might just possibly happen, add should after if: If it should rain, …. This sounds less certain and more polite than if it rains, and the main clause often has will, can or a request.

form.zh: If + 主语 + should + 动词原形, 主句
form.en: If + subject + should + base verb, main clause

pitfalls.zh: should 后用原形，别加 -s：不说 If he should comes。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb after should: If he should comes is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: if 从句里别再加 will：不说 If it should will rain。
pitfalls.en: Do not add will in the if clause: If it should will rain is wrong.

examples.text: If you should see him, please tell him I called.
examples.zh: 万一你见到他，请告诉他我来过电话。

examples.text: If it should snow tonight, the flight may be delayed.
examples.zh: 万一今晚下雪，航班可能会延误。

explain.zh: 讲到目前为止「已经被……」的事，用 have/has been + 过去分词。它把完成和被动合在一起：事情到现在做完了，而句子的重点落在承受动作的那一方，常和 since、already、recently 一起用。
explain.en: For something that has been done up to now, use have/has been + past participle. This joins the perfect with the passive: the action is complete by now, and the sentence focuses on the thing that receives it. It often goes with since, already and recently.

form.zh: have/has been + 过去分词；否定 have not been + 过去分词
form.en: have/has been + past participle; negative have not been + past participle

pitfalls.zh: been 不能省：不说 The room has cleaned。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop been: The room has cleaned is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 主语单数用 has，复数用 have，别弄反。
pitfalls.en: Use has with a singular subject and have with a plural one.

examples.text: The road has been closed since Monday.
examples.zh: 这条路从周一起就封闭了。

examples.text: All the tickets for the concert have been sold.
examples.zh: 音乐会的票已经全部卖完了。

explain.zh: 讲过去某一刻「正在被……」的事，用 was/were being + 过去分词。它强调当时那个动作还在进行，常和 when、at that time 这样的时间点一起出现。
explain.en: For something that was in the middle of being done at a past moment, use was/were being + past participle. It stresses that the action was still going on, and it often goes with a time point such as when or at that time.

form.zh: was/were being + 过去分词
form.en: was/were being + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 别漏 being：was repaired 是「修好了」，was being repaired 才是「正在修」。
pitfalls.en: Keep being: was repaired means it was fixed, was being repaired means it was still in progress.

pitfalls.zh: 主语是复数时用 were being，别一律写 was。
pitfalls.en: With a plural subject use were being, not was.

examples.text: The bridge was being built when we moved here.
examples.zh: 我们搬来时，那座桥正在修建。

examples.text: When I called, the room was being cleaned.
examples.zh: 我打电话的时候，房间正在打扫。

explain.zh: 讲一件更早的被动动作：在过去某事发生前，那个东西「已经被怎么样」了，就用 had been + 过去分词。它和过去完成时一样靠 had 提示时间，只是重点落在承受者身上，做事的人可以用 by 引出。
explain.en: Use had been + past participle for a passive action completed even earlier than another past event: by then the thing had already been done to it. As with the past perfect, had marks the earlier time, but the focus stays on whatever received the action, and by can name the doer.

form.zh: had been + 过去分词；否定 had not been done
form.en: had been + past participle; had not been done; Had it been done…?

pitfalls.zh: 别漏掉 been：had cleaned 就成了主动。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop been: had cleaned is active, not passive.

pitfalls.zh: 只讲更早的被动动作，别拿它代替一般过去时的被动。
pitfalls.en: Use it only for an earlier passive action, not instead of the ordinary past passive.

examples.text: When we reached the pool, it had already been cleaned.
examples.zh: 我们到泳池时，那里已经打扫过了。

examples.text: The window had been broken for weeks before anyone reported it.
examples.zh: 那扇窗破了几个星期才有人报告。

name.zh: 被动语态（间接宾语作主语）
name.en: PASSIVE: INDIRECT OBJECTS OF GIVE/PASS/SEND/SHOW/TEACH/TELL AS SUBJECTS

explain.zh: give、pass、send、show、teach、tell 这类动词带两个宾语。想把「谁收到了」放到最前面，就把人提上来作主语，后面接 was/were + 过去分词，原来的东西留在后面，不加 to。
explain.en: Verbs like give, pass, send, show, teach and tell take two objects. To put the receiver first, make the person the subject, follow it with was/were + past participle, and keep the thing at the end without to.

form.zh: 人 + be + 过去分词 + 东西（不加 to）
form.en: person + be + past participle + thing (no to); He was given a book.

pitfalls.zh: 后面的东西前不加 to：不说 was given to a book。
pitfalls.en: No to before the thing: not was given to a book.

pitfalls.zh: 只有这类带两个宾语的动词能这么变。
pitfalls.en: Only two-object verbs of this kind work this way.

examples.text: I was given a second chance to take the test.
examples.zh: 我得到了重考一次的机会。

examples.text: The new students were shown the library on their first day.
examples.zh: 新生第一天就被带着参观了图书馆。

name.zh: 被动语态（直接宾语作主语）
name.en: PASSIVE: DIRECT OBJECTS OF GIVE/PASS/SEND/SHOW/TEACH/TELL AS SUBJECTS

explain.zh: 还是 give、pass、send、show、teach、tell 这类动词，这次把被给、被送的那个东西提到句首作主语，人放到后面，前面加 to。想强调东西本身，或者人那一串太长时，就用这个说法。
explain.en: With the same verbs, you can instead put the thing that is given, sent or shown first as the subject, and place the person after to. Use this when the thing matters most or the person would make the subject very long.

form.zh: 东西 + be + 过去分词 + to + 人
form.en: thing + be + past participle + to + person; A book was given to him.

pitfalls.zh: 人前面别漏 to：不说 was given him。
pitfalls.en: Keep to before the person: not was given him.

pitfalls.zh: 东西作主语时动词跟东西走，别跟人。
pitfalls.en: The verb agrees with the thing, not with the person.

examples.text: The old letters were sent to a museum in Kyoto.
examples.zh: 那些旧信件被送去了京都的一家博物馆。

examples.text: A small prize was given to every child who finished.
examples.zh: 每个跑完的孩子都得到了一份小奖品。

name.zh: 完成式不定式 to have done

explain.zh: 要说「已经做过」或「比另一个动作更早完成」，用 to have + 过去分词。它常跟在 seem、appear、be said、be likely 后面，讲的是说话时已经结束的事。时间上它早于句子的主要动词。
explain.en: Use to have + past participle when the action was already finished, or finished earlier than another action. It often follows seem, appear, be said and be likely, and it points to something complete at the time we speak, earlier than the main verb.

form.zh: to have + 过去分词
form.en: to have + past participle; not to have done

pitfalls.zh: have 后面用过去分词，别写 to have did。
pitfalls.en: Use the past participle after have, not to have did.

pitfalls.zh: 它讲更早的事，别用来表示将来的完成。
pitfalls.en: It looks back, so do not use it for something finished in the future.

examples.text: She seems to have forgotten about our meeting.
examples.zh: 她好像把我们约好的事忘了。

examples.text: The train is said to have left an hour ago.
examples.zh: 据说那趟火车一小时前就开走了。

name.zh: 被动式不定式 to be done

explain.zh: 想说某件事「需要被做」或「将会被做」，用 to be + 过去分词。它常跟在 need、want、expect 后面，重点是动作落到谁或什么身上，做事的人不必说出来，要提就用 by。
explain.en: Use to be + past participle when something needs doing or will be done. It often follows need, want and expect. The focus is on what receives the action, so the doer can stay unmentioned, or be added with by.

form.zh: to be + 过去分词
form.en: to be + past participle; not to be done

pitfalls.zh: 别漏掉 be：不说 needs to cleaned。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop be: not needs to cleaned.

pitfalls.zh: 别照主动句补宾语：不说 to be cleaned the room。
pitfalls.en: Do not add an object as an active verb would take: not to be cleaned the room.

examples.text: The roof needs to be repaired before winter.
examples.zh: 屋顶得在入冬前修好。

examples.text: All these forms have to be signed by Friday.
examples.zh: 这些表格都得在周五前签字。

explain.zh: 马上就要发生的事，用 be about to + 动词原形，意思是「正要」。它比 be going to 更近，通常就是接下来几秒几分钟。常和 when 连用，说「正要……这时……」。
explain.en: Use be about to + base verb for something that will happen at once, meaning just about to. It is more immediate than be going to, usually within seconds or minutes, and it often pairs with when to set up an interruption.

form.zh: be about to + 动词原形
form.en: be about to + base verb; be changes form: was/were about to

pitfalls.zh: to 后面用原形，不说 about to leaving。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb after to, not about to leaving.

pitfalls.zh: 它已经表示马上，别再补 soon。
pitfalls.en: It already means very soon, so do not add soon.

examples.text: We were about to leave when the phone rang.
examples.zh: 我们正要出门，电话响了。

examples.text: She is about to start a new job in Osaka.
examples.zh: 她马上要在大阪开始一份新工作。

name.zh: 分词构句（-ed 置于句首）

explain.zh: 句首放一个 -ed 分词短语，交代主句主语「被怎么样」，相当于一个讲时间或原因的被动从句。分词说的是谁，必须就是主句主语。想换回完整句子，就补上 be 动词和 by。
explain.en: Start the sentence with a past-participle phrase to say what was done to the subject of the main clause, standing in for a passive clause of time or reason. The participle must share the subject of the main clause, and it can be rewritten as a full clause with be and by.

form.zh: 过去分词短语 + 逗号 + 主句；主语一致
form.en: past participle phrase + comma + main clause; same subject

pitfalls.zh: 分词说的必须就是主句主语，否则句子站不住。
pitfalls.en: The participle must describe the main clause subject, or the sentence falls apart.

pitfalls.zh: -ed 表被动或完成，别和 -ing 混用。
pitfalls.en: -ed marks passive or completed meaning; do not swap in -ing.

examples.text: Written in a hurry, the report still reads clearly.
examples.zh: 那份报告是赶着写的，读起来却很清楚。

examples.text: Surrounded by hills, the village stays quiet all year.
examples.zh: 村子四面环山，一整年都很安静。

explain.zh: 对过去已经发生、改不了的事表示后悔，用 wish + had + 过去分词，意思是「当时要是……就好了」。事实相反，所以说的是没做到的事。它只讲过去，别用来讲现在或将来。
explain.en: Use wish + had + past participle to express regret about something in the past that cannot be changed: I wish I had known. The opposite is what really happened, so the sentence is about what you did not do. It looks only backwards.

form.zh: wish + 主语 + had + 过去分词
form.en: wish + subject + had + past participle; I wish I had known.

pitfalls.zh: 讲过去的遗憾用 had done，别写 wish I knew。
pitfalls.en: For past regret use had done, not wish I knew.

pitfalls.zh: 别把它当成请求或许愿，它只表示后悔。
pitfalls.en: It is regret, not a request or a wish for the future.

examples.text: I wish I had brought a bigger bag.
examples.zh: 我真希望当时带了个大点儿的包。

examples.text: He wishes he had studied harder at school.
examples.zh: 他后悔上学时没更用功。

explain.zh: if only 加过去式，是对现在的情况不满或遗憾，意思是「要是现在……就好了」。事实和说的相反，所以动词退一步用过去式。语气比 wish 更重，常单独成句。
explain.en: If only with the past simple shows unhappiness or regret about the present: If only I had time. What you say is the opposite of the truth, so the verb steps back to the past. It is stronger than wish and often stands alone.

form.zh: If only + 主语 + 过去式
form.en: If only + subject + past simple; If only I had time.

pitfalls.zh: 讲现在的遗憾用过去式，别用 had done。
pitfalls.en: For a present regret use the past simple, not had done.

pitfalls.zh: if only 后面按正常语序，不用倒装。
pitfalls.en: Keep normal word order after if only; no inversion.

examples.text: If only I had more free time this month.
examples.zh: 这个月我要是有更多空闲就好了。

examples.text: If only we lived closer to the sea.
examples.zh: 我们要是住得离海近一点儿就好了。

explain.zh: if only 加 had + 过去分词，是对过去的遗憾，意思是「当时要是……就好了」。事情已经过去，改不了了，句子只在表达后悔。语气比平铺直叙重得多。
explain.en: If only with had + past participle expresses regret about the past: If only I had known. The moment is gone and nothing can change it, so the sentence only voices how sorry you are. The feeling is much stronger than a plain statement.

form.zh: If only + 主语 + had + 过去分词
form.en: If only + subject + had + past participle; If only I had known.

pitfalls.zh: 讲过去的遗憾才用 had done，别拿来讲现在。
pitfalls.en: Save had done for past regret; do not use it for the present.

pitfalls.zh: 别写 would have known，用 had known。
pitfalls.en: Say had known, not would have known.

examples.text: If only I had checked the address before leaving.
examples.zh: 出门前我要是核对一下地址就好了。

examples.text: If only she had said something at the meeting.
examples.zh: 她在会上要是说点什么就好了。

explain.zh: 说到将来某个时间点，某件事到那时已经持续了一段时间，用 will have been + 动词-ing。它强调的是「一直做了多久」，常和 by then、for ten years 一起出现。到那时动作多半还会继续。
explain.en: Use will have been + -ing for an action that will have gone on for some time by a point in the future. The point is how long it has lasted, and it often comes with by then or for ten years. The action usually continues after that point too.

form.zh: will have been + 动词-ing
form.en: will have been + -ing; will not have been -ing

pitfalls.zh: 别丢 been：不说 will have working。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop been: not will have working.

pitfalls.zh: 它强调持续，别用来单纯说将来做完。
pitfalls.en: It stresses duration, so do not use it just for finishing in the future.

examples.text: By June, I will have been teaching here for ten years.
examples.zh: 到六月，我就在这里教满十年了。

examples.text: Next month she will have been living in Osaka for a year.
examples.zh: 下个月她就在大阪住满一年了。

explain.zh: 讲一件事发生之前，主语已经被怎样对待了，就用 Having been + 过去分词 开头。它相当于把「先被……之后」压成一个短语，让主句的动作接着发生。这种说法多用于书面，主语必须和主句主语一致。
explain.en: Use Having been + past participle when, before the main action happens, the subject has already been dealt with in some way. The phrase squeezes 'after being ...' into one unit and lets the main clause follow. It belongs to written style, and its subject must be the same as the main clause subject.

form.zh: Having been + 过去分词，后接主句；否定 Not having been + 过去分词
form.en: Having been + past participle, then the main clause; negative Not having been + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 主语要一致：前后不是同一个人时，别用这个短语。
pitfalls.en: The subject must be shared: if the two clauses have different subjects, use a full clause instead.

pitfalls.zh: 别漏掉 been：不说 Having warned, she drove slowly。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop been: Having warned, she drove slowly is wrong.

examples.text: Having been warned about the ice, she drove very slowly.
examples.zh: 因为有人提醒过路面结冰，她开得很慢。

examples.text: Having been cleaned twice, the room smelled fresh again.
examples.zh: 房间已经擦过两遍，又清新起来了。

name.zh: 所有格 + -ing（动名词的逻辑主语）
name.en: V-ING: WITH NOTIONAL SUBJECT (expressed as possessive pronouns)

explain.zh: 想说某人做了某件事，而这件事本身是句子的话题，就把 my、his、their 这类所有格放在 -ing 前面。这个短语可以当主语，也可以放在动词或介词后面当宾语。口语里常把它换成 me、him 这样的宾格。
explain.en: When you want to name who does an action and make that action the topic of the sentence, put a possessive such as my, his or their before the -ing form. The phrase can be the subject, or the object of a verb or preposition. In casual speech the possessive often gives way to me or him.

form.zh: 所有格（my/his/their/Tom's）+ 动词-ing，可作主语或宾语
form.en: possessive (my/his/their/Tom's) + -ing, as subject or object

pitfalls.zh: 别用主格：不说 He coming late upset us。
pitfalls.en: Do not use the subject form: He coming late upset us is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 改成宾格后语气更随意，正式写作仍用所有格。
pitfalls.en: The object form sounds casual; keep the possessive in formal writing.

examples.text: His coming late to every meeting annoys the whole team.
examples.zh: 他每次开会都迟到，全队都很烦。

examples.text: We were surprised by her leaving so early.
examples.zh: 她这么早走，我们很意外。

explain.zh: 说没做某件事，又把这个动作放在动词后面当宾语，就在 -ing 前加 not。常用在 regret、mind、suggest、avoid 这类动词后面。not 只否定 -ing，不否定前面的动词。
explain.en: When you want to say that something was not done, and that action is the object of the verb, add not before the -ing form. It is common after verbs like regret, mind, suggest and avoid. The not negates only the -ing, not the verb before it.

form.zh: 动词 + not + 动词-ing；not 紧贴 -ing 之前
form.en: verb + not + -ing; not comes directly before the -ing form

pitfalls.zh: 别用 don't：不说 I regret don't going。
pitfalls.en: Do not use don't: I regret don't going is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: not 别挪到动词前：不说 I not regret going。
pitfalls.en: Keep not with the -ing: I not regret going is wrong.

examples.text: I regret not studying harder when I was at school.
examples.zh: 我后悔上学时没更用功。

examples.text: She suggested not telling anyone about the plan yet.
examples.zh: 她建议这个计划先别告诉任何人。

explain.zh: 猜一件事很可能会发生，就在 may 后面加 well，再接动词原形。well 不表示「好」，只把语气往「有充分理由这么想」上推。might well 意思相同，语气更弱一点。
explain.en: When you think something is very likely to happen, put well after may and then use the base verb. Well does not mean 'good' here; it pushes the sentence towards 'there is good reason to think so'. Might well means the same, a little softer.

form.zh: may / might + well + 动词原形
form.en: may / might + well + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 别把 well 换成 good：不说 It may good be true。
pitfalls.en: Use well, not good: It may good be true is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 别再加 to：不说 may well to rain。
pitfalls.en: Do not add to after well: may well to rain is wrong.

examples.text: The delay may well be caused by the heavy snow.
examples.zh: 这次延误很可能是大雪造成的。

examples.text: You may well be right about him.
examples.zh: 关于他，你很可能说对了。

name.zh: as if / as though + 过去完成式

explain.zh: 讲过去的事，说当时「好像曾经……」，而这个设想与事实相反，就用 as if / as though + had + 过去分词。它把想象的时间推到主句动作之前，让人觉得事情本该是另一个样子。
explain.en: To talk about the past and say that something seemed to have happened, when the idea is contrary to fact, use as if or as though + had + past participle. The imagined event is pushed back before the main verb, so the sentence suggests things should have been different.

form.zh: as if / as though + had + 过去分词
form.en: as if / as though + had + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 说现在不真实的假设别用它，改用一般过去式。
pitfalls.en: For an unreal idea about the present, use the past simple instead.

pitfalls.zh: had 后面只能接过去分词：不说 as if he had know。
pitfalls.en: Only a past participle follows had: as if he had know is wrong.

examples.text: He spoke as if he had seen the accident himself.
examples.zh: 他说得好像他亲眼见过那场事故。

examples.text: She looked at me as though I had said something wrong.
examples.zh: 她看着我，好像我说错了什么。

name.zh: if it were not for（若不是…）

explain.zh: 想说现在「要不是有某人某物，就会……」，用 If it were not for 加名词。后半句接 would 或 could 加动词原形，讲的是与现在事实相反的情况。
explain.en: To say that, as things stand now, something bad would happen without a particular person or thing, use If it were not for + noun. The second half takes would or could + base verb, because the situation is contrary to present fact.

form.zh: If it were not for + 名词，主句用 would/could + 动词原形
form.en: If it were not for + noun, would/could + base verb in the main clause

pitfalls.zh: 讲过去别用它，过去要用 had not been。
pitfalls.en: Do not use it for the past; the past needs had not been.

pitfalls.zh: 书面语里 were 别写成 was。
pitfalls.en: In writing, keep were; do not change it to was.

examples.text: If it were not for her help, we would still be stuck here.
examples.zh: 要不是她帮忙，我们还困在这儿。

examples.text: If it were not for the noise, I could work here all day.
examples.zh: 要不是这么吵，我能在这儿干一整天。

explain.zh: 把 If it were not for 里的 if 去掉，were 提到句首，就成了 Were it not for，意思完全一样。这种倒装更正式，多用在书面和演讲里。后面照样接名词和 would 加动词原形。
explain.en: Drop the if from If it were not for and move were to the front, and you get Were it not for, with exactly the same meaning. This inverted form is more formal and turns up in writing and speeches. A noun follows it, and the main clause still takes would + base verb.

form.zh: Were it not for + 名词，主句用 would/could + 动词原形
form.en: Were it not for + noun, would/could + base verb in the main clause

pitfalls.zh: 别在前面再加 if：不说 If were it not for。
pitfalls.en: Do not add if as well: If were it not for is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: were 别换成 was：不说 Was it not for。
pitfalls.en: Keep were: Was it not for is wrong.

examples.text: Were it not for the traffic, we would arrive by noon.
examples.zh: 要不是堵车，我们中午前就能到。

examples.text: Were it not for her patience, the team would fall apart.
examples.zh: 要不是她有耐心，这个团队早就散了。

name.zh: if it hadn't been for（若不是…）

explain.zh: 说过去的事「当时要不是因为……」，用 If it hadn't been for 加名词。主句用 would have 加过去分词，因为讲的是与过去事实相反的情况。
explain.en: For the past, when something bad did not happen only because of a person or thing, use If it hadn't been for + noun. The main clause takes would have + past participle, since the situation is contrary to what actually happened.

form.zh: If it hadn't been for + 名词，主句用 would have + 过去分词
form.en: If it hadn't been for + noun, would have + past participle in the main clause

pitfalls.zh: 讲现在别用它，现在要用 were not for。
pitfalls.en: Do not use it for the present; the present needs were not for.

pitfalls.zh: 主句别漏 have：不说 would missed the train。
pitfalls.en: Keep have in the main clause: would missed the train is wrong.

examples.text: If it hadn't been for the guard, the fire would have spread.
examples.zh: 要不是那个保安，火就烧开了。

examples.text: If it hadn't been for that phone call, I would have missed the train.
examples.zh: 要不是那个电话，我就错过火车了。

name.zh: had it not been for（倒装）

explain.zh: 把 If it hadn't been for 里的 if 去掉，had 提到句首，就成了 Had it not been for，意思不变。这是书面语的倒装说法，语气比带 if 的版本更正式、更紧凑。
explain.en: Drop the if from If it hadn't been for and put had first, and you get Had it not been for, with the same meaning. This is a written inversion: it sounds more formal and tighter than the version with if.

form.zh: Had it not been for + 名词，主句用 would have + 过去分词
form.en: Had it not been for + noun, would have + past participle in the main clause

pitfalls.zh: not 别放错位置：不说 Had it been not for。
pitfalls.en: Keep not after it: Had it been not for is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 前面别再留 if。
pitfalls.en: Do not keep if in front as well.

examples.text: Had it not been for your advice, I would have bought the wrong car.
examples.zh: 要不是你的建议，我就买错车了。

examples.text: Had it not been for the storm, the flight would have left on time.
examples.zh: 要不是那场暴风雨，航班就准点起飞了。

explain.zh: 说到将来某个时间点，某件事到那时会已经被做完，就用 will have been 加过去分词。句子常带 by 加将来时间，比如 by next June。主语是动作的承受者，不是执行者。
explain.en: When you look ahead to a point in the future and say that something will already be finished by then, use will have been + past participle. The sentence usually carries by + a future time, such as by next June. The subject receives the action rather than doing it.

form.zh: will have been + 过去分词；否定 will not have been + 过去分词
form.en: will have been + past participle; negative will not have been + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 别漏 been，否则就成了主动的将来完成。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop been, or the sentence turns into the active future perfect.

pitfalls.zh: 只跟 by 加将来时间搭配，别用 in 表截止。
pitfalls.en: Pair it with by + a future time, not in, for a deadline.

examples.text: By the end of May, all the roads will have been repaired.
examples.zh: 到五月底，所有道路都会修好。

examples.text: The results will have been published by Friday.
examples.zh: 结果会在周五前公布。

name.zh: 被动语态（情态 + 完成）

explain.zh: 猜过去发生的事，说它「一定已经」或「可能已经」被怎样了，就用 must、may、might、could 接 have been 加过去分词。这是对过去的推测，不是对现在的判断。
explain.en: When you guess about the past and say that something must have been or may have been done, use must, may, might or could + have been + past participle. The guess is about the past, not about the present.

form.zh: 情态动词（must/may/might/could）+ have been + 过去分词
form.en: modal (must/may/might/could) + have been + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 讲过去别只写 must be done，那只讲现在。
pitfalls.en: For the past, must be done is not enough; it speaks about now.

pitfalls.zh: been 别漏：不说 must have sent 表被动。
pitfalls.en: Do not drop been when the meaning is passive: must have sent is active.

examples.text: The letter must have been sent to the wrong address.
examples.zh: 那封信一定是寄到错误的地址了。

examples.text: The window might have been broken by the wind.
examples.zh: 窗户可能是被风吹破的。

name.zh: 完成被动式不定式 to have been done

explain.zh: 说一个动作在另一个动作之前就已经被做完，用 to have been 加过去分词。它常跟在 seem、appear、believe、report 这类词后面。时间上比句子的主谓语更早。
explain.en: Use to have been + past participle when an action was already completed before another action. It often follows verbs like seem, appear, believe and report. In time it sits earlier than the main verb of the sentence.

form.zh: to have been + 过去分词
form.en: to have been + past participle

pitfalls.zh: 只讲更早的事，别用它讲将来。
pitfalls.en: It points backwards in time; do not use it for the future.

pitfalls.zh: 别写成 to have being done。
pitfalls.en: The form is fixed: to have being done is wrong.

examples.text: The old theatre seems to have been closed for years.
examples.zh: 那座老剧院似乎已经关了好几年。

examples.text: He is said to have been chosen as the new coach.
examples.zh: 据说他被选为新教练了。

explain.zh: 想说做一件事是为了什么，就在主句后面加 so as to 加动词原形。它讲的目的是主句主语的打算，前后两个动作的主语要一致。要否定就说 so as not to。
explain.en: To say what purpose an action serves, add so as to + base verb after the main clause. The purpose belongs to the subject of the main clause, so both actions need the same subject. For a negative purpose, use so as not to.

form.zh: so as to + 动词原形；否定 so as not to + 动词原形
form.en: so as to + base verb; negative so as not to + base verb

pitfalls.zh: 别写成 so as to doing：to 后面用原形。
pitfalls.en: Use the base verb after to: so as to doing is wrong.

pitfalls.zh: 前后主语不同时别用它，改用 so that。
pitfalls.en: When the two subjects differ, use so that instead.

examples.text: She left early so as to catch the last bus.
examples.zh: 她提早离开，为了赶上末班车。

examples.text: He spoke quietly so as not to wake the baby.
examples.zh: 他说话很轻，以免吵醒孩子。
